a.title: XIVAPI search/Glasses bodies read with unbounded response.json(); item names have no length cap before the 7-day cache and the O(n^2) downstream sinks
a.deploy_unit: api-worker (primary); packages/core chara-gposers, packages/svg frame.ts, bot-logic/discord-worker and web-app as downstream sinks
a.reachable_path: Any client can POST /v1/chara/resolve and make searchItems (xivapi.ts:428-432) or getGlasses (:448-453) fetch from XIVAPI, but only the upstream (v2.xivapi.com or whatever host XIVAPI_BASE names) controls the body and name contents. A hostile or compromised upstream would send an oversized body or an oversized name, and that name is cached for about 7 days and served to web-app (chara-resolve-service.ts:212) and discord-worker (handlers/commands/glamour.ts:92), neither of which caps it.
a.why: The code matches the claim. xivapi.ts:432 and :453 call response.json() with no byte cap, while the context probe at :326-327 uses readBoundedText (32 KiB) and icons.ts:48 caps at 1 MiB. cleanName (:96-97) only strips U+00AD and trims, and namesOf (:184-190) does no slicing. The sinks are quadratic: gposers text() at chara-gposers.ts:120 uses /\s*[\r\n]+\s*/g, which backtracks O(n^2) on long whitespace runs, and fitText at frame.ts:185-202 pops one code point per iteration and re-measures the whole string each time. This is narrower than the MEDIUM/INTERNET-UNAUTH grading: the 2026-10-03 handoff (handoffs.md:217) routed it as robustness, the precondition is a malicious or compromised trusted upstream (redirects are refused at :396 and the base comes from a deploy var), and the impact stays within the affected item families (failed renders and wasted CPU), so this is LOW hardening rather than an exploitable weakness.
a.fix_direction:
Read both bodies with JSON.parse(await readBoundedText(response.body, MAX_SEARCH_BYTES)) (about 2 MiB for search, 32 KiB for Glasses). Map BodyTooLargeError to UpstreamUnavailableError so it is never cached.
In cleanName, strip C0/C1 control characters, collapse whitespace and cap names at about 128 code points before anything is cached.
Optional defense in depth: make fitText binary-search its cut point and rewrite gposers text() without the leading \s* backtracking.
a.evidence_excerpt: xivapi.ts:432 `const body = await response.json<RawSearchResponse>();` | :453 `const body = await response.json<RawSheetRow>();` | :97 `value.replace(/­/g, '').trim()` | vs :326-327 `JSON.parse(await readBoundedText(response.body, MAX_CONTEXT_BYTES))` | chara-gposers.ts:120 `value?.replace(/\s*[\r\n]+\s*/g, ' ')` | frame.ts:198 `while (chars.length > 1 && textWidth(chars.join('') + '…', size, font) > maxPx) chars.pop();`
a.preconditions: The attacker must control or compromise the XIVAPI upstream, or the XIVAPI_BASE var must be misconfigured to point at a hostile host. An internet client can trigger the fetch but cannot influence the body. All sub-claims are factually real (unbounded json at both sites, no name cap or control stripping, both quadratic sinks, no client-side cap), and the 7-day cache applies to rows that pass the identity check at :358-366.
a.variants: The other unbounded read in this unit is the cache read-back in chara/cache.ts:63 and :82 (response.json on our own cached rows). It is bounded by whatever was written, so the write-side cap fixes it too. A related consumer-side gap is core APIService.fetchWithTimeout, which checks size only after text() (handoff in the same 2026-10-03 list).
a.already_covered_by: Not covered by security-trade-offs.md or either prior report's positive controls. It was raised as an unfixed robustness handoff in docs/audits/2026-10-03-security/evidence/handoffs.md:217, which cited the then-current lines :280 and :294.
a.live_state_dependency: The production value of XIVAPI_BASE in wrangler.toml / deployed vars (the default is https://v2.xivapi.com). Whether XIVAPI itself enforces name lengths cannot be checked from the repo.

b.title: XIVAPI search/Glasses bodies read uncapped and names uncapped; harm requires a compromised XIVAPI upstream (hardening)
b.reachable_path: Any anonymous client can POST /v1/chara/resolve and cause searchItems (xivapi.ts:432) or getGlasses (:453) to fetch from XIVAPI, but the client controls only model keys, not the response. An oversized body or a long or whitespace-heavy name can come only from v2.xivapi.com, which is pinned in wrangler.toml:47/116 with redirects refused at xivapi.ts:387-398, so the precondition is an upstream compromise or a malicious upstream.
b.why: The code matches the claim: response.json() has no byte cap at :432 and :453, while the context probe is capped at 32 KiB (:164 and :326-327). cleanName (:96) only strips U+00AD and trims, and namesOf (:184-190) does not slice. The downstream sinks are really quadratic on long input: the gposers text() regex at packages/core/src/services/chara/chara-gposers.ts:120 on long whitespace runs, and the fitText pop+join loop at packages/svg/src/frame.ts:197-200. Rows are also cached about 7 days (cache.ts:22). No client-side trigger controls the content, though, and Workers memory and CPU limits bound the parse to a failed request. A compromised XIVAPI could already serve any wrong names (integrity is already trusted), so this is defense-in-depth hardening and not MEDIUM.
b.fix_direction:
Read the search and Glasses bodies with the existing lib/bounded-body.ts reader (or readBoundedText with a cap of a few hundred KiB, enough for a 500-row page), and refuse oversized bodies as UpstreamUnavailableError.
In namesOf/cleanName, strip C0/C1 controls, collapse whitespace, and cap each name at about 128 code points before caching.
Optionally make fitText binary-search its cut point and run gposers text() on capped input.
b.evidence_excerpt: xivapi.ts:432 `const body = await response.json<RawSearchResponse>();` / :453 `const body = await response.json<RawSheetRow>();` / :97 `value.replace(/­/g, '').trim()` vs :164 `MAX_CONTEXT_BYTES = 32 * 1024`; chara-gposers.ts:120 `/\s*[\r\n]+\s*/g`; frame.ts:198 `while (chars.length > 1 && textWidth(chars.join('') + '…', ...) > maxPx) chars.pop()`
b.preconditions: XIVAPI (v2.xivapi.com, pinned via the XIVAPI_BASE var) is compromised or malicious and returns an oversized body or an item or Glasses name of extreme length or whitespace. No end-user input can supply that content.
b.variants: Same unbounded-upstream-name pattern for the ITEM_FIELDS relation fields that parseItemRow passes through. Related: the 2026-10-03 handoff noted image-worker /extract has an uncapped c.req.json() (INTERNAL) and core APIService checks size only after text().
b.already_covered_by: Not an accepted trade-off. It was raised as a robustness handoff in docs/audits/2026-10-03-security/evidence/handoffs.md (trust-boundaries: "XIVAPI searchItems and getGlasses use an unbounded response.json()") and is still unfixed. It is absent from security-trade-offs.md and from the Positive controls / Rejected suspicions lists.
b.live_state_dependency: Production XIVAPI_BASE is the repo var https://v2.xivapi.com. The verdict assumes no dashboard override and that XIVAPI's real responses stay well below any proposed cap; the largest legitimate 500-row search page should be measured before choosing a cap.

a.title: Acting moderator's Discord username is written into persistent moderation-channel and submission-log posts, and neither privacy policy's list of post contents mentions it
a.reachable_path: A moderator in MODERATOR_IDS clicks Approve, Reject or Revert, submits a ban modal, or decides on a preview image. The handler copies interaction.member.user.username into an edited moderation-channel embed and, for approve/reject/revert, a new submission-log post.
a.why: The code does this: preset-moderation.ts:100 reads the username, then :180 sanitizes it and writes it at :220 ("Approved by") and :234 (submission-log). The same happens at preset-rejection.ts:162/177 (reject) and :307/322 (revert), at ban-reason.ts:200 ("Banned By"), and at discord-worker preview-image.ts:279/296-297, which falls back to the raw moderator ID when there is no username. Neither post-contents list mentions this field: apps/discord-worker/PRIVACY_POLICY.md:116 and its twin in apps/web-app/PRIVACY.md:147-157 both leave it out, and the policy's Moderation Records section (:57-58) names only moderator IDs in D1. I graded it below MEDIUM because the data subjects are the project's own moderators, whose names are shown only to other moderators in the two private staff channels. Their identity is already disclosed through the moderator ID in moderation_log, so the impact is a policy-completeness gap rather than exposure to other users.
a.fix_direction: Either name the field in the policies ("the name of the moderator who decided") or drop it from the embeds and attribute decisions through moderation_log alone. If you keep the name, also stop the preview-image fallback that prints the raw moderator ID (preview-image.ts:279), or disclose it too.
a.policy: AMEND apps/discord-worker/PRIVACY_POLICY.md section 5 "Where Your Data is Stored", Discord row (line 116), and apps/web-app/PRIVACY.md "Posts in our Discord server" bullet (lines 147-157). Alternative: NONE, if the name is dropped from the code.
a.variants: apps/discord-worker/PRIVACY_POLICY.{ja,de,fr,ko,zh}.md, section 5 Discord row; apps/web-app/PRIVACY.{ja,de,fr,ko,zh}.md, the Discord-posts bullet (the parity check is apps/web-app/src/__tests__/privacy-copy-parity.test.ts). Code sites: preset-moderation.ts:220,234; preset-rejection.ts:162,177,307,322; ban-reason.ts:200; discord-worker preview-image.ts:279,296-297 (locale keys previewImage.approvedFooter / previewImage.rejectedFooter in apps/discord-worker/src/locales/*.json; these are English-only admin strings).
a.evidence_excerpt: preset-moderation.ts:220 { name: 'Action', value: `Approved by ${safeModerator}`, inline: false }; :234 description: `Preset approved by ${safeModerator}`; PRIVACY_POLICY.md:116 lists preset, author name, reason, count and leaves out any moderator name.
a.preconditions: Requires a moderator in MODERATOR_IDS to act, and SUBMISSION_LOG_CHANNEL_ID to be set for the submission-log copy. Every sub-claim (approve, reject, revert, ban, preview-image) checks out in the code. One nuance the claim misses: the posts go only to private moderator channels, so the moderator's name is visible only to other moderators.
a.already_covered_by: Not covered. The prior FINDING-005 (2026-10-03) concerned ban/moderation-log D1 records and FINDING-007 concerned the author display name. Neither addressed the moderator's name in channel posts, and security-trade-offs.md has no matching entry.
a.live_state_dependency: Who can read the two channels (Discord server permissions) and whether SUBMISSION_LOG_CHANNEL_ID is set in production cannot be read from the repo.

b.title: Moderator's Discord username shown in moderation and submission-log posts; privacy policy's list of what those posts show leaves it out
b.deploy_unit: moderation-worker + discord-worker (policy text: discord-worker PRIVACY_POLICY + web-app PRIVACY)
b.reachable_path: A moderator listed in MODERATOR_IDS clicks Approve/Reject/Revert, submits a ban, or approves/rejects a preview image. The bot then edits the moderation-channel post and posts to SUBMISSION_LOG_CHANNEL_ID with that moderator's sanitized Discord username, e.g. "Approved by X" at preset-moderation.ts:220/:234, "Rejected by X" at preset-rejection.ts:162/:177, "Banned By" at ban-reason.ts:200, and preview-image.ts:279,296-297.
b.why: The code does what the reviewer says (userName comes from preset-moderation.ts:100). PRIVACY_POLICY.md:116 lists what the posts contain and leaves out the moderator name. Its Moderation Records section (:57-58) covers only moderator IDs, so the policy is incomplete. I graded it below MEDIUM for three reasons. The only people affected are the operator's own few moderators, acting in their staff role. The name goes only into the operator's two private channels, which the people named can read themselves, and it is their Discord username, which other members of that server can see anyway. The name is not written to D1, KV, logs or analytics: moderation_log keeps the ID, and presets-api reads X-User-Discord-Name at auth.ts:254 without storing it on these paths. So the effect is an incomplete but harmless policy, not new data being collected. One more detail: preview-image.ts:279 falls back to the moderator's numeric Discord ID when no username arrives. Discord always sends a username for guild button interactions, so this fallback is practically unreachable.
b.fix_direction: Option 1: keep the name for in-channel accountability and add one clause to the Discord row in each policy, e.g. "and the name of the moderator who decided". Option 2: replace it with a neutral label, "a moderator", and rely on moderation_log for accountability (policy NONE). Either way, drop preview-image.ts:279's fallback to moderatorId so no numeric ID can reach a post.
b.policy: AMEND apps/discord-worker/PRIVACY_POLICY.md §5 "Where Your Data is Stored", Discord row (:116), and apps/web-app/PRIVACY.md "Posts in our Discord server" (:147-159): add the deciding moderator's name. Alternatively fix the code to show a role label (policy NONE). The maintainer decides whether the name is needed.
b.evidence_excerpt: preset-moderation.ts:100 const userName = interaction.member?.user?.username ?? interaction.user?.username ?? 'Moderator'; :220 { name: 'Action', value: `Approved by ${safeModerator}` }; :234 description: `Preset approved by ${safeModerator}`; ban-reason.ts:200 { name: 'Banned By', value: safeModerator }; preview-image.ts:279 const displayName = sanitizeEmbedText(moderatorName, MODERATOR_NAME_MAX) || moderatorId;
b.preconditions: The actor must be in MODERATOR_IDS. The submission-log post happens only when SUBMISSION_LOG_CHANNEL_ID is set.
b.variants: apps/discord-worker/PRIVACY_POLICY.{ja,de,fr,ko,zh}.md (§5 Discord row); apps/web-app/PRIVACY.md :147-159 and apps/web-app/PRIVACY.{ja,de,fr,ko,zh}.md (same "Posts in our Discord server" bullet). Code sites: preset-moderation.ts:220,234; preset-rejection.ts:162,177,307,322; ban-reason.ts:200; discord-worker preview-image.ts:279,296-297 (previewImage.approvedFooter / rejectedFooter in en.json).

a.title: /glamour embed's plain() leaves masked-link syntax in upstream item names and acquisition lines unescaped
a.reachable_path: Any Discord user runs /glamour with a .chara file. The worker posts a public embed whose description holds item names that api-worker fetched live from XIVAPI (apps/api-worker/src/chara/xivapi.ts:186-189, cleanName strips only soft hyphens) and acquisition lines from the bundled acquisition.en.json, all passed through plain() at glamour.ts:412, 581, 591 and 598. If an upstream name were poisoned to contain [text](https://evil), it would render as a clickable masked link.
a.why: plain() at glamour.ts:384-386 escapes only * _ ~ ` | \, and its doc comment (378-383) says leaving brackets and parentheses unescaped is deliberate. The safer escapeDiscordMarkdown/defuseMentions helpers in discord-markdown.ts are not used here. Exploiting this needs XIVAPI or the build-time acquisition table to be compromised: no string from the user's file reaches these sinks (missing items show only the numeric formatCharaModelLabel), committed data has 0 "](" and 0 mention tokens, mentions inside embeds never ping, and # or > only take effect at line start, which needs a newline injected into the name. That makes this upstream-trust hardening with a phishing-link ceiling, so LOW.
a.fix_direction: In plain(), also escape [ and ] (enough to break masked links without the paren backslashes the comment wants to avoid), defuse <@…>/<#…>/<t:…>/@everyone, and collapse \r\n to a space. Alternatively, have api-worker's cleanName reject or strip those tokens at the source. Add a test with a "[x](https://e)" name.
a.preconditions: A third party (XIVAPI) is compromised, or the build-time acquisition/regional-name data is poisoned. Both reviewers' sub-claims hold. The mention-ping part has no effect because embeds never ping and edits pin allowed_mentions to none. The heading/blockquote part also needs an injected newline, because each value follows a bold label on its line.
a.evidence_excerpt: glamour.ts:385 `return text.replace(/([*_~`|\\])/g, '\\$1');` ; xivapi.ts:97 `value.replace(/­/g, '').trim()`
a.variants: Same sink for glasses names (Facewear line via gposersList) and the fixed/blocked/company notes. The web reader is out of scope here.
a.already_covered_by: Not covered: no matching entry in security-trade-offs.md or in either prior audit report. The only record of the trade-off is the code comment at glamour.ts:378-383.
a.live_state_dependency: Live XIVAPI response content (third party); the repo cannot show whether current upstream names contain markup.

b.title: /glamour embed's plain() leaves masked-link, heading and mention-token markdown in upstream item and acquisition names
b.reachable_path: An attacker who controls what v2.xivapi.com returns for an item or glasses Name (or who can change the build-time acquisition/ko/zh tables) gets a string into the api-worker /v1/chara/resolve answer. Any Discord user who then runs /glamour with a .chara file wearing that piece gets a public embed with that text, passed through plain() only (glamour.ts:412, :581, :591, :598), and discord-worker posts result.embed.description unchanged (apps/discord-worker/src/handlers/commands/glamour.ts:189).
b.why: plain() at glamour.ts:384-386 escapes only * _ ~ ` | and backslash. Upstream names reach it with no character filtering: xivapi.ts:96-97 cleanName only strips soft hyphens and trims, and the handler adds no sanitizeEmbedText on the success path. So a name like [text](https://evil) renders as a masked link, and # or > renders as a heading or quote. The impact is limited: discord-api.ts:84/108 sends allowed_mentions parse [] by default, so <@id> or @everyone never pings; Discord's leaving-Discord prompt shows the real host; this requires compromising a third party or the repo; and no "](" appears in the committed data today. No security-trade-offs or 2026-10-03/10-15 positive-control entry covers it. The only rationale is the code comment at :377-383.
b.fix_direction: In plain(), also break masked links and mention tokens without hurting ordinary parentheses: escape [ and ] (or just the "](" sequence), and add a leading-#/> escape plus bot-logic's defuseMentions for <@ <# <t: and @everyone/@here. Add a glamour.test.ts case that pins a [x](https://e) name rendering inert.
b.evidence_excerpt: glamour.ts:384-386 function plain(text) { return text.replace(/([*_~`|\\])/g, '\\$1'); } — used at :412 (GPOSERS values incl. acquisition), :581, :591, :598; discord-worker glamour.ts:189 description: result.embed.description (no sanitize); api-worker xivapi.ts:96-97 cleanName strips only U+00AD.
b.preconditions: Upstream poisoning: v2.xivapi.com (third party) or its source serves a crafted Name, or the repo's build-time acquisition.en.json / item-names.{ko,zh}.json carry one. Committed data has no "](" today.
b.variants: Both member rows describe the same sink (gap-upstream-game-data-trust-02, r2-bot-chara-second-look-02). Affected inputs are item names (en/ja/de/fr from XIVAPI at run time, ko/zh from bundled tables), glasses names via localName (:563), and acquisition lines in the GPOSERS list. Mention tokens render but do not ping because of allowed_mentions parse [].
b.already_covered_by: Not covered: docs/architecture/security-trade-offs.md and the 2026-10-03 / 2026-10-15 SECURITY_AUDIT_REPORT positive controls contain no entry for this. The only rationale is the in-code comment at glamour.ts:377-383.
b.live_state_dependency: The live XIVAPI_BASE / XIVAPI_VERSION values and whatever v2.xivapi.com serves now; api-worker's edge cache would keep a poisoned row after the upstream is fixed.

a.title: Swatch 'Save character colors' always names its local kind:'character' record after the .chara nickname/file name; PRIVACY.md describes the fallback only for glamour/palette saves and wrongly says character saves have no delete control
a.deploy_unit: web-app (code + PRIVACY.md and its 5 locale siblings)
a.reachable_path: A user loads a .chara in the Swatch Matcher and clicks "Save character colors" (chara-file-card.ts:364-375 → swatch-tool.ts:1385 onSaveCharacter → saveCharacterColors). The record is created with no name prompt, named `nickname.trim() || fileName || 'Character colors'` (chara-sheet.ts:210-214, createCollection at :223), and written to that browser's localStorage only.
a.why: Code confirmed: unlike the glamour palette save (glamour-block.ts:1816-1825, which takes a typed draft first), the Swatch character save has no name field, so every save holds the nickname or file name. PRIVACY.md:36-40 discloses that fallback only for "a glamour or its palette" saved "without typing a name". PRIVACY.md:61-62 does name Swatch character saves but not the nickname, and its "no delete control" claim is false: Manage Collections (dye-selector.ts:563-565 → collection-manager-modal.ts:22 getCollections(), all kinds; delete :198, rename :460) is reachable from the Accessibility, Comparison, Harmony and Mixer dye selectors. That corrects web-app-chara-01's "no way to remove it" sub-claim. The name never leaves the device or reaches a log (the logger at :232 logs counts only). Not covered by prior audits: the 2026-10-03 positive control (line 114) covers logs, datapoints, KV keys and outbound bodies, not local record names.
a.fix_direction: Minimize: name the character record with the localized default (swatch.characterDefaultName) and numbering via uniqueCollectionName, or add a name field like the glamour save, which starts empty. Then fix PRIVACY.md 'What is stored on your device' line 61-62: character colors can be renamed and deleted through Manage Collections in any dye selector. If the nickname fallback is kept, AMEND 'Character files' to name the Swatch character save.
a.policy: NONE for the nickname, which serves no purpose here (fix the code; a default name works). CORRECT apps/web-app/PRIVACY.md 'What is stored on your device' (lines 61-62, Swatch character colors do have a delete/rename control via Manage Collections). If the code is not changed instead, AMEND apps/web-app/PRIVACY.md 'Character files' (lines 36-40) to cover the Swatch character save.
a.variants: apps/web-app/PRIVACY.md, PRIVACY.ja.md, PRIVACY.de.md, PRIVACY.fr.md, PRIVACY.ko.md, PRIVACY.zh.md: same two sections in each. Every collection name, nickname-derived ones included, also lands in the user-initiated Export All JSON download (collection-manager-modal.ts:517). That download is local, but the policy does not mention it either.
a.preconditions: User imports a .chara with a nickname or a meaningful file name and clicks Save character colors; impact confined to that user's own browser storage (shared-device readers of localStorage).

a.title: Unpinned preview_urls on the presets-api / moderation-worker dev workers (production D1/R2/KV, ENVIRONMENT=development)
a.reachable_path: None from the repo. Even then, the unsigned-bot arm still requires the dev worker's BOT_API_SECRET bearer (auth.ts:268).

a.title: FINDING-023 still open: production and beta Discord bot tokens remain repository-scope Actions secrets 21 days after the deletion precondition was met
a.reachable_path: Someone with write access pushes a workflow on any branch that references secrets.DISCORD_TOKEN or MODERATION_DISCORD_TOKEN with no environment:. The repository-scope copy resolves, so the main-only branch policy on the production environment never applies.
a.why: A live GET of actions/secrets on 2026-10-26 still lists DISCORD_TOKEN (2026-05-26), MODERATION_DISCORD_TOKEN, BETA_DISCORD_TOKEN and BETA_DISCORD_GUILD_ID at repository scope. The production environment also holds DISCORD_TOKEN and MODERATION_DISCORD_TOKEN, and its only branch policy is main. The deletion precondition in OPEN_ITEMS.md:44-49 is met: every job that reads these tokens declares environment: (deploy-discord-worker.yml:50/94, deploy-moderation-worker.yml:45/87, sync-dye-emojis.yml:36/53, deploy-discord-worker-beta.yml:122/185), and the last three production deploys of both workers succeeded on main on 2026-10-26. Despite that, SECRET_ROTATION.md:64 and DEPLOY_ENVIRONMENTS.md:121-124 describe the tokens as environment secrets with no repository copy left; this is the open carry-over of FINDING-023, not an accepted trade-off. Severity stays LOW: the only collaborator is the one admin, fork pull requests get no secrets, and nothing in the repo shows whether the May repository DISCORD_TOKEN value still works.
a.fix_direction:
Maintainer: run gh secret delete DISCORD_TOKEN, MODERATION_DISCORD_TOKEN, BETA_DISCORD_TOKEN and BETA_DISCORD_GUILD_ID at repository scope, then check off OPEN_ITEMS.md FINDING-023 with the date.
Optionally reset the bot token if the repository DISCORD_TOKEN value still differs from the environment one and is valid.
a.preconditions: Write access to the repository (one admin, FlashGalatine). It also requires that the repository copy of the token is still valid: the repository DISCORD_TOKEN was last updated 2026-05-26 and the environment copy 2026-10-05, so if the bot token was reset on 10-05 the repository copy is dead for the main bot.
a.live_state_dependency: Whether the repository-scope DISCORD_TOKEN (2026-05-26) and MODERATION_DISCORD_TOKEN (2026-08-29) values are still valid Discord bot tokens cannot be read; GitHub secret values are write-only.

OPEN_ITEMS.md:47 says "Still to do: delete the four repository copies".

a.title: Author-ban guard on approve/revert is a separate, non-atomic pre-read in moderation-worker; presets-api /status and /revert write approved with no author-ban check
a.reachable_path: A moderator clicks Approve (or submits a Revert) on a banned author's pending/flagged preset while a second moderator's ban of that author commits between the isPresetAuthorBanned read and the PATCH. Separately, any moderator can send PATCH /api/v1/moderation/:id/status or /revert straight to api.xivdyetools.app with a web JWT, which skips the pre-check entirely.
a.why: processApproval reads isPresetAuthorBanned (preset-moderation.ts:186) and then calls presetApi.approvePreset (:206); processRevert does the same (modals/preset-rejection.ts:268 then :293). presets-api's /status batch (moderation.ts:225, prepareStatusUpdate in preset-service.ts) and /revert batch (moderation.ts:330, prepareRevert) bind only id/status/revision/snapshot, with no banned_users lookup. requireNotBanned is mounted only on presets.ts:131 and votes.ts:30 and checks the caller, not the author. banUser's batch (ban-service.ts:508, hideUserPresetsStatement :678-688) hides only 'approved' rows, so a write that lands after the ban leaves that preset public. Real but bounded: it needs moderator privileges (trusted MODERATOR_IDS) or a narrow two-moderator race, affects one preset, and any moderator can reject it again. Not covered by security-trade-offs.md or the 2026-10-03 or 2026-10-15 positive controls.
a.fix_direction: Enforce the author ban inside the presets-api write itself by adding `AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM banned_users b WHERE (b.discord_id = presets.author_discord_id OR b.xivauth_id = presets.author_discord_id) AND b.unbanned_at IS NULL)` to the WHERE clause of prepareStatusUpdate (when the target status is approved) and of prepareRevert. Map the zero-row case to a distinct 409 or 403 AUTHOR_BANNED, and keep moderation-worker's pre-check only for UX.
a.preconditions: Actor holds moderator rights (MODERATOR_IDS). Either two moderators act on the same author within one request's latency (ban commits between pre-read and PATCH), or a moderator calls the presets-api moderation route directly instead of through the bot. The slash-command path (commands/preset.ts:284) only gates a confirmation; its button re-checks at preset-moderation.ts:186, so it carries the same window.
a.variants: apps/moderation-worker/src/handlers/modals/preset-rejection.ts:268->293 (revert); apps/moderation-worker/src/handlers/commands/preset.ts:284 (pre-confirm check); apps/presets-api/src/handlers/moderation.ts:225 (/status) and :330 (/revert); apps/presets-api/src/services/preset-service.ts prepareStatusUpdate / prepareRevert
a.evidence_excerpt: preset-moderation.ts:186 `if (await banService.isPresetAuthorBanned(env.DB, presetId)) {` ... :206 `await presetApi.approvePreset(env, presetId, userId, binding)`; preset-service.ts `WHERE id = ? AND status = ? AND content_revision = ?`; ban-service.ts:686-688 `WHERE author_discord_id = ? AND status = 'approved'`
a.live_state_dependency: Membership of the MODERATOR_IDS secret, which decides who can take the direct-API path.
a.already_covered_by: Partially: MOD-4 / FINDING-034 (2026-08-21 audit) added the pre-check, but only on the moderation-worker side and not atomically. No accepted trade-off or rejected suspicion covers this.

b.title: Ban check on approve/revert runs only in moderation-worker and is not atomic with the write. presets-api's status and revert routes do not check whether the author is banned.
b.reachable_path: Only a moderator can reach this: the routes are gated by requireModerator (presets-api moderation.ts:163, :260; MODERATOR_IDS), and the caller must hold the moderator's bot-signed or web-JWT identity. Moderator A approves or reverts a banned author's pending preset in the roughly 100 ms between isPresetAuthorBanned (preset-moderation.ts:186, preset-rejection.ts:268) and the PATCH (:206, :293), while moderator B commits banUser in that same window. A moderator who calls presets-api directly can also skip the pre-check.
b.why: The code matches the claim. prepareStatusUpdate (preset-service.ts:458-464) and prepareRevert (:481-486) bind only id, status, revision and snapshot, with no lookup in banned_users. The ban hides only presets that are 'approved' (ban-service.ts:686-688), so a pending row keeps its revision and the race goes through. The claim overstates the threat: no untrusted principal can trigger or time this. A banned author cannot submit or edit (requireNotBanned), and the result is a preset that a trusted moderator reviewed and approved on purpose, which any moderator can reject again. That makes this a moderator-on-moderator consistency gap and defense-in-depth hardening, not an exploitable weakness.
b.fix_direction: Make the check atomic on the server. a.title: Tags and example_link are never content-moderated, so an approved preset can carry or gain arbitrary tag text without review or a daily cap; looping such edits also keeps moderator reject/revert returning STALE_REVIEW
a.reachable_path: A logged-in user (web JWT or signed bot interaction) POSTs a preset with a clean name and description but offensive tags, which is auto-approved. Or the user PATCHes {"tags":[...]} / example_link on their own approved preset, which stays approved, sends no notification and uses no daily slot; repeating that about once a second bumps content_revision, so a moderator's reject or revert, bound to a revision read before the confirm click and modal, gets 409 STALE_REVIEW.
a.why: The submit path moderates only name and description (presets.ts:1031-1036), and the edit path sets textChanged from name/description alone (presets.ts:653-655). reserveDailyEvent('text_edit') runs only inside if(textChanged) (:665-700), and ownerEditOutcome('approved', not flagged) writes no status and notifies nobody (:533-536). The TAG_PATTERN comment (validation-service.ts:157-159) confirms tags are never moderated, but the pattern still allows any letters, so slurs pass. The 0014 trigger bumps content_revision on changes to tags, example_link, category and secondary_categories, and moderator /status and /revert compare it (preset-service.ts:461 and :485), so the STALE_REVIEW loop is also real. The impact is bounded: the per-user limit is 100/min, the ban hide (a direct D1 update in moderation-worker ban-service) and moderator DELETE are not bound to a revision, and example_link must point to an allowlisted host.
a.fix_direction: Pass tags (joined) and the example_link path to moderateContent on submit and whenever they change on edit. Treat a tag or link change like a text change for the text_edit quota and for the approved→pending flip. Optionally let a moderator take down a preset without a revision check (a hide/flag action that is not bound to the reviewed revision).
a.evidence_excerpt: presets.ts:653-655 `const textChanged = (body.name !== undefined && body.name !== preset.name) || (body.description !== undefined && body.description !== preset.description);` ; :533-536 `case 'approved': return flaggedByThisEdit ? {pending,true} : { nextStatus: undefined, notifiesModerators: false };` ; :1031 `moderateContent(body.name, body.description, ...)` ; migrations/0014 trigger `AFTER UPDATE OF ... tags, ... example_link, secondary_categories`

a.variants: Submit path (presets.ts:1031), where an offensive tag set is auto-approved at creation within the 10/day submission cap. The same lack of moderation applies to category_id and secondary_categories edits, which are allowlisted values and harmless on their own but still bump the revision.
a.already_covered_by: Not covered. This is the residual of 2026-08-21 PAPI-6, which was folded into FINDING-019 and marked FIXED on the tag charset rule only. Adding tags to moderation never landed. It is not listed in security-trade-offs.md or in the positive controls of 2026-10-03 or 2026-10-15.

The poisoned names then ship in /v1/chara/resolve answers and /glamour cards after the next api-worker deploy.

Add a content gate that rejects names containing C0/C1 controls, bidi overrides or over-long values (U+200F is already allow-listed in discord-worker's coverage test).

a.title: /glamour has no tier of its own and spends one shared api-worker service key
a.reachable_path: Any Discord user runs /glamour with a .chara attachment. That is up to 15 runs a minute per account (the default tier) and each run makes one POST /v1/chara/resolve over the UNIVERSALIS_PROXY binding. About 87 accounts together fill api-worker's single 'workers' service bucket (1300/60 s), after which every user's /glamour answers RESOLVE_BUSY.

Every binding request has no client IP, so api-worker rate-limit.ts:61-62,97 puts them all under one key, 'workers', limited to 1300/60 s (wrangler SERVICE_RATE_LIMITER, limit 1300). glamour.ts:54-98 makes one resolve per run, and bot-logic glamour.ts:468-470 turns a 429 into RESOLVE_BUSY. The effect is cross-user availability only: no data exposure, and the public /v1/chara/resolve already allows 60/min per IP, so it adds no new amplifier.

a.preconditions: The attacker needs about 87 Discord accounts that can run the bot's commands, each sending a valid .chara attachment (the attachment guards run before the defer). Native rate limits are counted per colo, but Discord interactions arrive from Discord's own egress, so in practice the bucket is close to global for the bot.
a.live_state_dependency: How many colos Discord interaction traffic lands in decides whether the 1300/60 s bucket is effectively global. The deployed SERVICE_RATE_LIMITER namespace 1005 (limit 1300) is assumed to match wrangler.toml.
a.variants: Any future service-binding caller of /v1/* shares the same 'workers' key (rate-limit.ts:62). Today /glamour is the only one; /budget's Universalis routes use their own UNIVERSALIS_SERVICE_RATE_LIMITER.

b.title: Bot fleet shares one api-worker service key (1300/60 s), so about 87 Discord accounts at the 15/min default can make /glamour answer "busy" for every user
b.reachable_path: About 87 Discord accounts each run /glamour with a .chara attachment 15 times a minute. Discord delivers interactions from concentrated infrastructure, so the bot most likely runs in very few colos, which makes this easier for an attacker, not harder. The claim is narrower than its headline: "no tier of its own" is immaterial, because the default of 15/min equals the /swatch tier, and the shared aggregate ceiling is the intended design (rate-limit.ts:50-59 comment, wrangler.toml:67 "discord-worker limits each user itself"). Alternatively, record the shared-key availability trade-off in docs/architecture/security-trade-offs.md. a.title: POST /presets spends a Perspective call before reserving quota; a same-dye concurrent burst is charged one submission
a.reachable_path: A logged-in user (web JWT, or a bot-signed request) sends a burst of concurrent POST /api/v1/presets with the same fresh dye set and clean name/description. Every request passes the read-only cap check (:998) and the duplicate pre-check (:1025) before the first INSERT lands, so each one calls moderateContent/Perspective (:1031). The losers then hit the dye_signature UNIQUE collision (:1058) and return through respondToDuplicate (:171-205) without writing a submission_events row.

Perspective's quota is about 1 QPS, so the burst drives it to 429, and other users' submissions and edits fall to perspective_unavailable, then pending (moderation-service.ts:280-285). This fails closed, so nothing gets published unmoderated, but auto-approval and the moderator queue are degraded. It also contradicts security-trade-offs.md:309, which says "one account cannot drive Perspective to 429"; only PATCH reserves first (reserveDailyEvent at presets.ts:683), so this is not an accepted trade-off.
a.fix_direction: Reserve a 'submission' slot with reserveDailyEvent before moderateContent in POST (reserve-then-act, never released), the same pattern PATCH uses for text_edit, and keep the BUG-049 post-insert recount as a backstop. Then update security-trade-offs.md mitigation 2 / Code References to name the POST reservation.
a.preconditions: PERSPECTIVE_API_KEY is set in production. The attacker has a valid account that is not banned and has daily submission quota left. The burst requests arrive inside the first request's Perspective latency window (up to the 5 s timeout), and the name/description pass the local word list so they reach Perspective. A narrower variant needs no same-dye trick: concurrent distinct-dye POSTs also spend Perspective before they are charged. Each of those is charged afterward through the event plus the rollback, though, so it allows only one burst per account per day.

a.title: No cache-miss upstream budget on /v1/chara/*; arbitrary canonical icon ?version= (and any unknown key) forces an XIVAPI call per request
a.reachable_path: An anonymous client sends GET /v1/chara/icon/:id?version=<any 16-hex> (router.ts:306-314 accepts it, xivapi.ts:294-296 marks it cacheable unchecked), or POST /v1/chara/resolve with novel set/base/variant integers. Each one is a cache-cold key and costs one XIVAPI asset fetch or search (plus a Glasses fetch) under the project User-Agent. The only limit is the shared /v1/* bucket of 65 per 60 s per IP per colo, which fails open.
a.why: Every fact holds at HEAD. resolveAssetContext (xivapi.ts:294-296) trusts any canonical version, and the icon cache key includes that version (icon-cache.ts:28). The resolve keys pack any integer lane up to LANE_MAX (router.ts:60-73, 118-120), and lookup-loader.ts:58-62 stores every non-truncated miss for about 7+1 days. The chara routes have no miss-only limiter of the kind the Universalis proxy got in FINDING-011 (no chara hit for a miss limiter in src). A 429 only throws to a 503 with no backoff (xivapi.ts:399-400), and API_LIMIT is failOpen: true (rate-limit.ts:31). The new ?version= adds little: an unversioned unknown iconId already ends in an uncached 404 (icons.ts:35), and resolve keys are already attacker-chosen. The real weakness is the missing miss budget, which is bounded to about 1-2 upstream calls per admitted request per IP. The impact is bounded: XIVAPI could throttle or block the shared User-Agent, which would degrade the chara feature for all users. No prior audit or trade-off doc covers this (the 2026-10-03 note was evidence-only, not in Rejected suspicions).
a.fix_direction: Charge only cache misses on /v1/chara/* to a dedicated per-IP native rate-limit binding (mirror the Universalis onMiss pattern, with a 20x service key for discord-worker's /glamour). Optionally accept ?version= only when it equals the currently discovered or pinned game key, or serve it uncacheable otherwise. Add a short circuit-breaker on upstream 429/503.
a.preconditions: Any internet client. Amplification scales with the number of source IPs and colos, because the 65/60 s counter is per IP per colo and admits on backend error. Unconfirmed: how XIVAPI answers an unknown version key. The upstream call happens either way, and only a 200 PNG gets cached.
a.variants: The same missing miss budget covers POST /v1/chara/resolve (search + Glasses fetch per novel lookup set) and GET /v1/chara/icon/:id without ?version= (an unknown iconId 404 is never cached).
a.evidence_excerpt: xivapi.ts:295-296 `const version = versionOverride ?? this.version; if (isCanonicalVersion(version)) return { base: this.base, version, cacheable: true };` | rate-limit.ts:31 `failOpen: true` | icons.ts:35 404 thrown, never cached
a.live_state_dependency: How XIVAPI rate-limits or blocks the project's User-Agent, and how it answers an unknown asset version key. Whether API_RATE_LIMITER is bound in production (the repo's wrangler.toml declares it).
a.already_covered_by: Not covered. FINDING-011 (2026-10-03) added a miss limiter to the Universalis proxy only. The 2026-10-03 review-api-worker-chara-universalis-telemetry.md:57 note is evidence-only, not a filed finding and not a rejection.

b.title: /v1/chara/* relays every cold-key request to XIVAPI 1:1 under the project UA, with only the shared 65/60 s per-IP bucket and no 429 backoff (?version= adds no new bypass)
b.reachable_path: Any anonymous client sends GET /v1/chara/icon/<id>?version=<16hex> or POST /v1/chara/resolve with unseen (slot, base, variant) keys. Each request misses the cache and makes at most one XIVAPI asset fetch (icons.ts:25), or one search plus at most one Glasses read (router.ts:200-235), under the rate-limit.ts:31/wrangler.toml:55 bucket of 65 per 60 s per IP.

But ?version= opens no new bypass: CANONICAL_ICON_ID (router.ts:55) already gave about 999,999 cold icon keys per request, and the resolve key space was already caller-chosen. The 2026-10-03 reviewer saw that resolve-side pollution and left it unfiled, and amplification is at most 2 upstream calls per request at about 1 request/s per IP, so a single client is no worse than calling XIVAPI directly. What is left is hardening for a distributed caller: there is no miss-only budget like Universalis's FINDING-011, and an upstream 429 produces a 503 without backoff (xivapi.ts:399-400), so XIVAPI could throttle the project's User-Agent.
b.fix_direction: Optionally add a miss-only per-IP limiter on /v1/chara/* (charge only on loader.loadRows/loadGlasses/fetchIcon). Add a short per-isolate cooldown after an upstream 429/503. Optionally accept only the current or last-known game version for cacheable icon keys and treat others as uncached.

b.live_state_dependency: How XIVAPI v2 rate-limits or blocks by User-Agent or source, and how it answers an unknown version key. Whether the API_RATE_LIMITER binding is bound in production (if it is not, the fallback is KV, which fails open).
b.preconditions: The caller needs many source IPs to reach a volume that would matter to XIVAPI. A single IP is capped at 65 requests/min with at most 2 upstream calls each.

b.reachable_path: Any internet client sends GET /universalis/aggregated/<unknown-name>/1 (or /api/v2/...), which runs cachedFetch on the fixed keys 'data-centers:all' and 'worlds:all' with no onMiss (router.ts:192-216). a.title: 16-bit PNG within the pixel cap overruns the isolate memory limit (pixel budget assumes 4 B/px)
a.reachable_path: A Discord user attaches a ~73 KB 3072x3072 16-bit RGBA PNG to /extractor (discord-worker image-client.ts:53 -> image-worker POST /extract), or a signed-in preset author uploads it as a preview image (presets-api preview-image-service.ts:143 -> POST /thumbnail, under its 5 MB gate). Both reach processImageForExtraction / processImageForThumbnail, whose only pre-decode gate is assertImageDimensionsFromHeader (validators.ts:302) -> validateDimensions (281-283), which passes at exactly MAX_PIXEL_COUNT.
a.why: MAX_PIXEL_COUNT (validators.ts:104-106) is 72 MiB / (4 B x 2 copies), and readPng (dimensions.ts:46-50) reads only width/height, never bit depth or color type; nothing in image-worker, discord-worker or presets-api checks bit depth. I reproduced this independently with the repo's @cf-wasm/photon 0.4.0 in Node (wasm memory hooked): a 3072x3072 PNG grows wasm linear memory to 110.25 MiB at 8-bit, 146.88 MiB at 16-bit RGBA (73,452 B file) and 128.88 MiB at 16-bit RGB. That is over the 128 MiB isolate limit before any JS buffers are counted, and wasm memory never shrinks. The effect is bounded to availability: the isolate is killed and the attacker's request plus any concurrent /extract or /thumbnail on that isolate fail. There is no data exposure, so LOW stands, and an authenticated sender is required. Side note: even the 8-bit peak at the cap (110 MiB of wasm alone) contradicts the "peak near 95-100 MB" comment at validators.ts:77-79.
a.fix_direction: Read the PNG IHDR bit depth (byte 24) and color type (byte 25) in dimensions.ts. Either refuse 16-bit input or charge it a bytes-per-pixel factor of 2x or more against the pixel budget. Then re-measure the real wasm peak (8-bit at the cap is already 110 MiB) and lower PIXEL_MEMORY_BUDGET_BYTES until it leaves real headroom, with a regression test on a 16-bit PNG at the cap.
a.evidence_excerpt: validators.ts:104 MAX_PIXEL_COUNT = floor(PIXEL_MEMORY_BUDGET_BYTES / (BYTES_PER_RGBA_PIXEL * CONCURRENT_RGBA_COPIES)); dimensions.ts:46 readPng returns ok(u32be(b,16), u32be(b,20)) with no bit-depth read. Verifier probe (scratchpad g17/probe.mjs), wasm memory after new_from_byteslice: 8-bit 3072^2 = 110.25 MiB; 16-bit RGBA = 146.88 MiB; 16-bit RGB = 128.88 MiB.
a.preconditions: The sender needs a Discord account (a signed interaction) for /extractor, or a valid user JWT for a preset preview upload. The precondition is that workerd counts wasm linear memory against the 128 MiB isolate limit and enforces it the way Node's growth figures suggest. The figures were measured in Node, not workerd.
a.variants: The /extract route (photon.ts processImageForExtraction) and the /thumbnail route (processImageForThumbnail) share the same decode and the same gate. 16-bit RGB (color type 2) also lands over the limit at 128.88 MiB. 8-bit RGBA at the cap reaches 110 MiB of wasm, which leaves thin margin once the up to 10 MB source buffer and runtime overhead are added. The validators.ts:74-80 comment and the image-worker CLAUDE.md "peak 95-100 MB" claim need correcting.
a.live_state_dependency: This depends on how workerd and Cloudflare production actually enforce the 128 MiB per-isolate limit against wasm memory: whether the isolate is killed mid-request or after it completes. It could not be run under workerd here.
a.already_covered_by: Not covered. The 2026-10-03 and 2026-10-15 reports and security-trade-offs.md do not mention bit depth. BUG-052 and FINDING-004 (pre-decode gate) address only pixel count and side length.

b.title: 16-bit PNG within MAX_PIXEL_COUNT decodes to ~147 MiB of photon wasm memory, over the 128 MiB isolate limit (pixel budget assumes 4 B/px, bit depth never read)
b.reachable_path: A Discord user runs /extractor with a ~73 KB 3072x3072 16-bit RGBA PNG attachment (discord-worker extractor.ts:497 -> image-client.ts:53 -> /extract), or an authenticated preset author uploads one as a preview image (presets-api -> /thumbnail). Both hit assertImageDimensionsFromHeader (photon.ts:187 / :279), which passes at exactly MAX_PIXEL_COUNT, then PhotonImage.new_from_byteslice (photon.ts:87) decodes it.
b.why: MAX_PIXEL_COUNT (validators.ts:104-106) is 72 MiB / (4 B x 2 copies), but readPng (dimensions.ts:46-50) ignores IHDR bit depth and nothing else checks it. My own independent probe against the real @cf-wasm/photon 0.4.0 found the same numbers as the reviewer: 3072x3072 RGBA peaks at 110.25 MiB of wasm linear memory at 8-bit and 146.88 MiB at 16-bit, on both the extract and thumbnail paths. A 16-bit 3840x2160 image (129.38 MiB) is also over the limit. Wasm growth is set by the module's own allocator, so it should be the same in workerd. The impact is limited to transient availability: the isolate is killed and concurrent /extract and /thumbnail calls fail. The callers are auth-gated and rate-limited, no data is exposed, and nothing in security-trade-offs.md or the earlier audit reports covers this.
b.fix_direction: In dimensions.ts readPng, return the IHDR bit depth (byte 24). Then in validateDimensions, either reject 16-bit PNGs or weight the pixel count by bytes per sample (for example, halve the cap for depth 16). Add a gate test with a 16-bit IHDR at the cap. Also re-measure the 8-bit peak (110 MiB), since the "95-100 MB" comment at validators.ts:77-79 understates it.
b.policy: NONE (availability hardening, no personal data or policy text involved)
b.evidence_excerpt: Independent probe (scratchpad g17/probe.mjs, real photon 0.4.0, Node): 3072x3072 RGBA depth 8 -> 110.25 MiB peak wasm; depth 16 -> 146.88 MiB (file 73,452 B); 3840x2160 depth 16 -> 129.38 MiB; thumbnail path same 146.88 MiB. validators.ts:104 `MAX_PIXEL_COUNT = Math.floor(PIXEL_MEMORY_BUDGET_BYTES / (BYTES_PER_RGBA_PIXEL * CONCURRENT_RGBA_COPIES))`; dimensions.ts:46-50 readPng reads only width/height.
b.preconditions: The caller has a signed Discord interaction (and is under discord-worker's per-user command rate limit), or is an authenticated presets-api author. The 16-bit PNG is served unmodified from cdn.discordapp.com, or uploaded directly within presets-api's 5 MB / PNG-sniff gate.
b.variants: 16-bit RGB (color type 2) and 16-bit gray+alpha PNGs within the cap behave the same way. The /thumbnail path (processImageForThumbnail, photon.ts:277-279) has the same peak. Even the 8-bit peak at the cap (110 MiB) leaves a thin margin for the JS heap.
b.live_state_dependency: I measured in Node and could not run workerd. The exact Cloudflare behaviour on exceeding 128 MiB (killing the isolate vs failing only the request) and its effect on in-flight requests on the same isolate are platform runtime behaviour I could not observe.
b.already_covered_by: Not covered. The 2026-10-03 report (line 115) lists the header dimension gate only as a positive control and does not consider bit depth. Nothing in security-trade-offs.md covers it.

a.title: Logger: a non-Error `error` argument skips key-name redaction (cookie, session_id, webhook_url, set_cookie, auth_header, nested keys)
a.deploy_unit: logger (published @xivdyetools/logger; consumed by every worker via worker-kit, plus discord/moderation/stoat directly)
a.reachable_path: A Worker code path calls `logger.error(msg, <plain object>)`, or catches a thrown non-Error object, and passes it in the `error` slot. createEntry (base-logger.ts:231-232) sends it to formatError, whose non-Error branch (:277-281) runs safeStringify and then only the free-text SANITIZE_RULES, never redactSensitiveFields.
a.why: Confirmed at base-logger.ts:275-281 (the reviewer cited 268, which is the stack check in the Error branch). Free-text rules still catch quoted keys ending in token/secret/password/key (:952), plus authorization and the other key=value rules. Keys such as cookie, set_cookie, session_id, webhook_url and auth_header (CORE_REDACT_FIELDS) are emitted verbatim, while the same object passed as context is redacted. The cited call sites (discord-worker index.ts:319/:916, moderation-worker :239, presets-api retention-job.ts:86, stoat-worker index.ts:70) are actually all `logger.error(msg, {ctx})` with harmless values, and the web-app wrapper routes plain objects into context. That makes this a misuse trap with no live leak, and Workers Logs are off by wrangler.toml.
a.fix_direction: In formatError's non-Error branch, run a plain object through redactSensitiveFields (the full context pipeline) before safeStringify, so the key-name list and SENSITIVE_SUFFIX apply. Optionally fix the five call sites to `logger.error(msg, undefined, ctx)`. Add a test pinning cookie/session_id/nested keys in the error slot.
a.rotation: None. No secret is shown to have been logged.
a.preconditions: A developer or upstream library passes or throws a non-Error object that carries a cookie, session_id, webhook_url, set_cookie or auth_header key. No current in-repo call site does this with sensitive values. Output goes only to console / wrangler tail, since Workers Logs are disabled.
a.variants: Same branch applies to a thrown string (free-text rules only, which is expected). Five context-as-error call sites: apps/discord-worker/src/index.ts:319, :916; apps/moderation-worker/src/index.ts:239 (also :355, :541, :574 same shape); apps/presets-api/src/retention-job.ts:86; apps/stoat-worker/src/index.ts:70 (also :97, message-handler.ts:139).
a.live_state_dependency: Whether Workers Logs / Logpush are truly off in the Cloudflare dashboard. The repo pins [observability] enabled=false and the workers:check-logs gate enforces it.
a.evidence_excerpt: base-logger.ts:277-281: `const raw = typeof error === 'string' ? error : safeStringify(error); return { name: 'Unknown', message: this.config.sanitizeErrors ? this.sanitizeErrorMessage(raw) : raw };`
a.already_covered_by: Not covered. Not in security-trade-offs.md or the 2026-10-03 / 2026-10-15 positive controls. FINDING-026 only added free-text sanitizing to this branch.

b.title: Logger: a non-Error `error` argument gets only the free-text rules, not key-name redaction (latent misuse trap, no live leak)
b.reachable_path: A worker calls `logger.error(msg, x)` where `x` is a plain object, either a context passed in the wrong slot or a thrown non-Error object. `formatError` (base-logger.ts:277-281) then runs `safeStringify` plus `SANITIZE_RULES` only, without `redactSensitiveFields`.
b.why: The mechanism is real. Line 277 sends a non-Error through `safeStringify` and `sanitizeErrorMessage` only. The JSON sweep (line 952) catches only quoted keys ending in token/secret/password/key, and the `authorization` rule catches only that key, so `cookie`, `set_cookie`, `session_id`, `webhook_url` and `auth_header` pass through verbatim. Every cited call site is real and passes harmless values: discord-worker index.ts:319 `{minimum}` and :916 `{commandName}`, moderation-worker :239/:355/:541/:574 `{commandName|customId}`, and presets-api retention-job.ts:86 `{failed}` (prune names). stoat-worker index.ts:70 sends only `error.message`, and web-app's wrapper (apps/web-app/src/shared/logger.ts error()) passes only real Errors to that slot, so today nothing personal or secret reaches this path and there is no direct effect, below the claimed LOW.
b.fix_direction: In formatError's non-Error branch, when the value is a non-null object, run `this.redactSensitiveFields(value)` (with a fresh guard) before `safeStringify`, then apply the free-text rules. Optionally move the context-shaped call sites (discord-worker index.ts:319/:916, moderation-worker :239/:355/:541/:574, retention-job.ts:86) to `logger.error(msg, undefined, ctx)` so their fields land in `context`. Add a hardening.test.ts case: `log.error('x', {cookie:'c', nested:{session_id:'s'}})` must emit neither value.
b.evidence_excerpt: base-logger.ts:277-281: `const raw = typeof error === 'string' ? error : safeStringify(error); return { name: 'Unknown', message: this.config.sanitizeErrors ? this.sanitizeErrorMessage(raw) : raw };`. Key-name redaction exists only in redactSensitiveFields (line 388-392), which formatError never calls. base-logger.test.ts:307-314 pins `{custom:'error'}` serialised as the message, but no test covers sensitive key names in this slot.
b.preconditions: A caller must pass an object carrying a sensitive key name (cookie/session_id/webhook_url/set_cookie/auth_header) as the 2nd `error` argument, or a library must throw such a non-Error object into a `logger.error(msg, e)` catch block. Workers Logs must also be on: every wrangler.toml pins observability off (workers:check-logs gate). With `sanitizeErrors: false` (dev) even the free-text rules are skipped.
b.variants: Same slot: the 7 in-repo call sites that put a context object in the error position (discord-worker src/index.ts:319, :916; moderation-worker src/index.ts:239, :355, :541, :574; presets-api src/retention-job.ts:86). The reviewer listed stoat-worker index.ts:70, but that site passes a context-shaped object whose only field is `error.message`, so it carries no extra keys.
b.live_state_dependency: Whether Workers Logs/Logpush are actually disabled in the Cloudflare dashboard. The repo pins `[observability] enabled = false` in each wrangler.toml.
b.already_covered_by: Not covered. FINDING-026 (non-Error throws sanitised) addressed free-text only, and neither the 2026-10-03 nor the 2026-10-15 audit nor security-trade-offs.md lists the key-name gap for the error slot.

a.title: sanitizeEmbedText omits bidi isolates U+2066-2069, Arabic letter mark U+061C and tag block U+E0000-E007F
a.reachable_path: A Discord user includes U+2066-2069 / U+061C / tag characters in a slash-command option (dye search query, /budget world or dye, color input) or in a .chara field that /swatch or /glamour echoes in an error, and the bot echoes it through sanitizeEmbedText unchanged. Stored preset name, description, tags and author reach embeds too, but presets-api already rejects or strips U+2066-2069 for those fields, so through that path only U+061C and the tag characters get through.
a.why: The INVISIBLE class at discord-markdown.ts:22-26 does leave out U+2066-2069, U+061C and U+E0000-E007F, although the docblocks at lines 18-21 and 53-55 say bidi controls are stripped. The claim overstates the reach and the impact. presets-api already refuses bidi isolates in stored preset fields (apps/presets-api/src/services/validation-service.ts:77 INVISIBLE_CHARS with U+2066-2069, enforced at :149 and in sanitizeAuthorName :120-122), and moderator names are Discord usernames, which have a restricted charset. RLO/LRO/RLE/LRE (U+202A-202E) are stripped, so these characters cannot reverse Latin letters: isolates and ALM only reorder neutral and number runs, and tag characters only add invisible padding to the user's own echoed input or a stored preset field.
a.fix_direction: Add ؜, ⁦-⁩ and the tag block (\u{E0000}-\u{E007F}, which needs the 'u' flag) to INVISIBLE in packages/bot-logic/src/discord-markdown.ts, and add the same ranges to the copy in apps/stoat-worker/src/services/response-formatter.ts:83-86. Optionally add U+061C and the tag block to presets-api INVISIBLE_CHARS too. Add test cases covering each range.
a.preconditions: The attacker can invoke bot commands, which needs a signed Discord interaction, or can submit a preset, which needs an OAuth JWT. Through stored preset fields only U+061C and the tag characters get through, because isolates are refused upstream. Echoes of a user's own command input mainly reach that same user, or the channel when the response is not ephemeral.
a.variants: apps/stoat-worker/src/services/response-formatter.ts:83-86 duplicates the same INVISIBLE class with the same gaps (that app is parked). apps/presets-api/src/services/validation-service.ts:77 covers the isolates but not U+061C or the tag block.
a.live_state_dependency: Preset rows stored in D1 before presets-api added its isolate rule (2026-10-03 FINDING-016) could still contain U+2066-2069. The repo does not show this.
a.already_covered_by: Partly covered: presets-api validation-service.ts:77/:149 (preset fields) and sanitizeAuthorName :120 (author) already refuse or strip U+2066-2069 at the store layer. Not listed as an accepted trade-off.

b.title: sanitizeEmbedText misses bidi isolates (U+2066-2069), ALM (U+061C) and tag characters (U+E0000-E007F)
b.reachable_path: A Discord user puts U+2066-2069 or U+061C in a slash-command option that is echoed back (/dye search query, /budget world, colour inputs, /changelog version), or a moderator's display name contains them. A preset author can also put U+061C or tag characters in a stored preset name or description, which then reaches other users' embeds.
b.why: A probe with the INVISIBLE class at discord-markdown.ts:22-26 removes only U+202E from 'a⁦b⁧c⁩d؜e\u{E0041}f‮g' (14 -> 13 code units), so the docblock's promise to strip bidi controls is wrong for isolates. The impact is narrower than claimed. presets-api already rejects isolates in name and description and strips them from author_name (validation-service.ts:77, 189, 218, 120-138), and TAG_PATTERN (line 159) blocks every format character in tags, so for stored presets only U+061C and the invisible tag block get through. The isolate vector that remains is mostly users echoing their own text. U+202A-202E, which does the real reversal, is already stripped, so isolates and ALM only move neutral characters and digits, and tag characters only hide text.
b.fix_direction:
Add ؜, ⁦-⁩ and \u{E0000}-\u{E007F} to INVISIBLE in discord-markdown.ts. The regex needs the 'u' flag for the astral range. Pin this with a bot-logic test.
Optionally add U+061C and the tag block to presets-api INVISIBLE_CHARS (validation-service.ts:77) as well, so both layers agree.
b.preconditions: The attacker can invoke slash commands (a signed Discord interaction), or is a preset author with a valid JWT or bot identity. The effect is cosmetic: neutral characters or digits are reordered, or text is hidden, inside the attacker's own string.
b.variants: presets-api INVISIBLE_CHARS (apps/presets-api/src/services/validation-service.ts:77) also omits U+061C and U+E0000-E007F. discord-worker sanitize.test.ts:205 tests only U+202E/U+200E/U+2063, so nothing pins the gap.
b.already_covered_by: Not covered. The 2026-10-03 report's positive controls (SECURITY_AUDIT_REPORT.md:109) only say that user text goes through sanitizeEmbedText, not that its character set is complete. FINDING-016/028 (presets-api character rules) already close the isolate vector for stored preset fields.
b.live_state_dependency: Whether Discord's client strips or isolates these code points in slash-option values or embed fields was not checked. The verdict rests on the repo alone.

a.title: sanitizeEmbedText leaves Discord <...> syntax (channel, slash-command, emoji, timestamp, guild-nav) live in bot-voiced embeds
a.reachable_path: An authenticated user submits a community preset (or author name) such as "</ban:123> <#456>" through /preset submit or the web app. presets-api accepts it, and discord-worker's /preset list (preset.ts:238, embed description) and preset notifications render it through sanitizePresetName/sanitizePresetDescription, which wrap sanitizeEmbedText.
a.why: MARKDOWN_SPECIALS at line 15 is /([*_~`|>#\\[\]()])/g with no '<', and defuseMentions (lines 46-50) only rewrites @everyone/@here and <@id>/<@!id>/<@&id>. So <#id>, </cmd:id>, <:e:id>, <t:...> and <id:customize> still render as live channel links, slash-command mentions, emoji, timestamps or guild navigation in bot-authored embed descriptions and field values. presets-api validation-service.ts:184-221 checks only length and control/invisible characters, so '<' reaches the sink. No ping is possible (ALLOWED_MENTIONS_NONE on every payload, discord-api.ts:31-32), so the impact is bounded bot-voiced spoofing and misdirection, which FINDING-019 meant to close.
a.fix_direction: Add '<' to MARKDOWN_SPECIALS (Discord shows a literal \< and kills every <...> form), keeping defuseMentions first. Add tests for <#id>, </cmd:id>, <:e:id>, <t:0> and <id:customize>. Then bump bot-logic, publish it, and redeploy both bots.
a.preconditions: Needs a valid Discord identity or JWT to submit a preset. Presets that wait for moderation are seen only after approval, though the moderator embeds render the text too. The echo sinks (budget, dye, harmony and others) are mostly ephemeral replies to the user's own input, so self-only.
a.variants: One fix covers all callers. Other sinks are moderation-worker utils/embed-text.ts:27-53 (moderator-facing preset name, description, user and reason), discord-worker preset-notifications.ts:132-166 and preview-image.ts:279. stoat-worker response-formatter.ts:116 uses the same sanitizer, but Revolt syntax differs and that unit is parked.
a.already_covered_by: Not covered. FINDING-019 (2026-08-21) introduced this sanitizer but defused only <@...>. No entry in security-trade-offs.md or the 2026-10-03 or 2026-10-15 positive controls or rejected suspicions.
a.live_state_dependency: Discord client rendering of <#id>, </cmd:id> and <t:...> inside embed descriptions and field values (they do not render in embed titles).

b.title: escapeDiscordMarkdown leaves Discord angle-bracket tokens (<#id>, </cmd:id>, <id:...>, <:e:id>, <t:...>) live in bot-voiced embeds
b.reachable_path: An authenticated preset author (web JWT or /preset submit) puts e.g. `</preset show:123>` or `<t:0:R>` or `<#channelId>` in a preset name/description; presets-api validatePresetName/Description (apps/presets-api/src/services/validation-service.ts:174-223) only rejects control/invisible characters, so `<` is stored. Once approved (auto-approved when the moderation scorer passes it), other users' `/preset show` / list embeds render it via sanitizePresetDescription -> sanitizeEmbedText (apps/discord-worker/src/handlers/commands/preset.ts:1020, :238), which leaves `<` unescaped.
b.why: Line 15's MARKDOWN_SPECIALS class covers `>` but not `<`, and defuseMentions (lines 46-50) only rewrites `@everyone/@here` and `<@!?&?digits>`. That leaves channel, slash-command, guild-navigation, custom-emoji and timestamp tokens live in embed descriptions and field values. No upstream guard exists: presets-api allows `<`, the only test (discord-markdown.test.ts:41-45) covers just `<@&...>`, and neither the 2026-10-03 nor the 2026-10-15 report nor security-trade-offs.md mentions this gap (the 2026-10-03 positive control only says sanitizeEmbedText is applied). The impact stays bounded: allowed_mentions is none so nothing pings, masked links stay escaped so no hidden URL, and a slash mention only prefills a command for the user who clicks it. That makes it bot-voiced cosmetic spoofing, i.e. LOW.
b.fix_direction: Add `<` to MARKDOWN_SPECIALS so `\<` renders literally (Discord honours the backslash). Alternatively, defuse every `<[@#:/a]...>` / `<t:...>` / `<id:...>` token the way `<@id>` already is. Pin it in discord-markdown.test.ts with `<#1>`, `</x:1>`, `<id:customize>`, `<:e:1>` and `<t:0:R>` cases.
b.preconditions: The attacker needs an authenticated preset submission that gets approved (manual or auto), or they can only echo text back to themselves through the command-input error paths (budget, dye, harmony and so on).
b.variants: The same sanitizer feeds moderation-worker (apps/moderation-worker/src/utils/embed-text.ts:27-53), the discord-worker moderation webhook embed (preset-notifications.ts:154-166) and stoat-worker (response-formatter.ts:116; Revolt syntax differs, and that bot is parked). One fix in bot-logic covers all of them.
b.live_state_dependency: Whether presets auto-approve depends on PERSPECTIVE_API_KEY being set in production. Without it, every text goes to manual moderator review, and a moderator then sees the rendered token too.
b.already_covered_by: Not covered. The 2026-08-21 FINDING-019 remediation introduced this sanitizer but scoped mention handling to `<@...>` only.

a.title: Beta bot's presets-api access rests on an unenforced "omit the bot secrets" convention, and DEPLOY_ENVIRONMENTS.md:284 contradicts it
a.reachable_path: Someone with push access to the repo pushes a non-main branch that touches discord-worker, and deploy-discord-worker-beta.yml:17-22 deploys it to xivdyetools-discord-worker-dev, which binds the production presets-api (wrangler.toml:29-31, service xivdyetools-presets-api = [env.production] name at presets-api wrangler.toml:69). Only if the maintainer set BOT_API_SECRET and BOT_SIGNING_SECRET on the -dev worker can that code send v2-signed requests with any X-User-Discord-ID and get isModerator (auth.ts:335-345).
a.why: The mechanics are real. Any holder of the signing pair can claim any X-User-Discord-ID and gets moderator rights for the IDs in MODERATOR_IDS (auth.ts:341). Without the pair, production presets-api treats beta as unauthenticated (auth.ts:262-291; preset-api.ts:88 sends no Bearer when the secret is unset), so DEPLOY_ENVIRONMENTS.md:284's "writes a genuine row" claim either describes a state the runbook (:324) and wrangler.toml:92-96 say is optional, or it reveals that beta holds the pair. This adds almost no risk on top of what is already accepted: pushing a branch needs repo write access, and the beta Cloudflare token already carries account-wide Workers Scripts Edit (DEPLOY_ENVIRONMENTS.md:88-102), so a malicious branch could deploy arbitrary code to the production workers directly. What is left is doc and config hygiene, and whether the beta secrets exist can't be checked from the repo.
a.fix_direction: Change DEPLOY_ENVIRONMENTS.md:284 and :324 (and the discord-worker wrangler.toml:92-96 comment) to say BOT_API_SECRET/BOT_SIGNING_SECRET MUST NOT be set on -dev, and drop or reword the "writes a genuine row" residual-risk line. Have the maintainer run `wrangler secret list` on xivdyetools-discord-worker-dev and delete the pair if it is there. Optionally, have discord-worker validateEnv warn when ENVIRONMENT=development carries BOT_SIGNING_SECRET.
a.rotation: Only if `wrangler secret list` shows BOT_API_SECRET/BOT_SIGNING_SECRET on xivdyetools-discord-worker-dev: rotate both on presets-api, discord-worker and moderation-worker production, and delete them from -dev.
a.preconditions: Repo push access (maintainer-level) AND BOT_API_SECRET+BOT_SIGNING_SECRET set on the -dev worker. Neither the repo nor any workflow sets them, and wrangler.toml:92-96 says beta needs only DISCORD_TOKEN+DISCORD_PUBLIC_KEY. The same push access plus CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN_BETA (Workers Scripts Edit, account-wide) already allows deploying to the production workers.
a.evidence_excerpt: auth.ts:273 isDevOrTest gate (prod presets-api ENVIRONMENT=production, wrangler.toml:76); auth.ts:341 isModerator: checkModerator(userDiscordId, ...) after verifyBotSignatureV2 + nonce; DEPLOY_ENVIRONMENTS.md:284 "Accepted residual risk: /preset submit from beta writes a genuine row"; :324 "Optional secrets (BOT_API_SECRET, INTERNAL_WEBHOOK_SECRET) may be omitted" (BOT_SIGNING_SECRET unmentioned)
a.already_covered_by: 2026-08-29 audit DW-14 (INFO, evidence/review-discord-worker.md:241, :279): it recommended changing the "may be omitted" wording to "must not be set", and that change was never made. Not listed in the 2026-10-03 or 2026-10-15 positive controls or rejected suspicions, so it is not excluded on that ground.
a.live_state_dependency: Cloudflare secrets on xivdyetools-discord-worker-dev (wrangler secret list): whether BOT_API_SECRET/BOT_SIGNING_SECRET are present. If they are, severity is still LOW, because the beta CF token's account-wide Workers Scripts Edit already gives push-access holders a more direct route to production.
a.variants: Same pattern in moderation-worker's dev block, which binds the production D1/KV (2026-08-29 MOD-06); worth checking in the same pass.

b.title: Nothing stops the beta bot from holding production's presets-api signing pair, and the docs contradict each other on whether it does
b.reachable_path: Only someone who can push a branch to FlashGalatine/xivdyetools can reach this (fork PRs do not fire `push`). Their branch code runs as xivdyetools-discord-worker-dev, which is bound to production presets-api (wrangler.toml:29-31). It gains moderator-equivalent bot auth only if a human has run `wrangler secret put` for the production BOT_API_SECRET and BOT_SIGNING_SECRET on that -dev worker.
b.why: The mechanism checks out. The bot path in presets-api (auth.ts ~335-342) trusts any X-User-Discord-ID that is HMAC-signed with the pair and derives isModerator from MODERATOR_IDS. Without the secrets, preset-api.ts:88-127 sends no Authorization header and production presets-api rejects unsigned bot auth (auth.ts ~275-290), so by default beta can only read. The repo does not show the precondition: wrangler.toml:92-96 and DEPLOY_ENVIRONMENTS.md:324 call the secrets unneeded or optional. The real defect is narrower: :284 and :399 accept that beta writes live rows, which is only possible with the production pair. :324 still says "may be omitted" rather than "must not be set", which the 08-21 and 08-29 audits asked to tighten (DW-14, INFO), and no code refuses the pair on a non-production deployment.
b.fix_direction:
In discord-worker validateEnv, refuse to start (or drop PRESETS_API writes) when ENVIRONMENT !== 'production' and BOT_API_SECRET or BOT_SIGNING_SECRET is set, and pin this with a test.
Correct DEPLOY_ENVIRONMENTS.md :284/:399 (beta preset writes 401 without the pair) and change :324 to say the bot secrets must never be set on -dev.
Run `wrangler secret list` on xivdyetools-discord-worker-dev; if the pair is there, delete it and rotate.
b.rotation: Only if the live check finds BOT_API_SECRET/BOT_SIGNING_SECRET on xivdyetools-discord-worker-dev: delete them there, then rotate the pair on presets-api, discord-worker and moderation-worker production (--env production) per SECRET_ROTATION.md. Otherwise none.

a.deploy_unit: oauth (only oauth; every other wrangler.toml keeps routes solely under [env.production], or overrides them there in og-worker's case)
a.reachable_path: A maintainer or agent runs `wrangler deploy --env development` from apps/oauth once the dev D1 id is filled in. It sets no privacy or security promise and has no exploitable effect, and a normal browsing user never reaches 100/min, so it rates INFO, not LOW.
