a.title: Upstream XIVAuth email auto-merge attaches a new provider identity to the email-matched account and signs in without MFA, so oauth mints a JWT with the victim's discord_id
a.deploy_unit: gap (upstream XIVAuth a4e6693; impact lands in apps/oauth + apps/presets-api)
a.reachable_path: An attacker without an XIVAuth session signs in at /auth/sso/{discord|github|twitch} with a provider account whose verified email equals the victim's XIVAuth email. find_user_by_authdata (:101-117) has no (provider, uid) match, so it falls back to the email lookup, builds the identity on the victim's user and calls sign_in_and_redirect (:60-62), skipping MFA. The attacker then completes the xivdyetools oauth flow as the victim and gets a presets-api JWT carrying the victim's discord_id.
a.why: At :109-116, when no (provider, uid) identity exists, the code looks up the user by email, add_social_identity builds the identity, and :62 signs the user in. The MFA prompt exists only on the password path (sessions_controller.rb:136-140; mfa_enabled? at user.rb:75), and no global Warden hook enforces it. Downstream, oauth finds the row by xivauth_id (user-service.ts:73-77) and puts its discord_id in the JWT (jwt-service.ts:141), which presets-api treats as the acting id and moderator id (auth.ts:361-365). The rating stays LOW because every in-tree login provider passes only a verified email (discord.rb:23 and patreon.rb by source; omniauth-github and twitch with user:email / user:read:email return verified emails per their gem and API docs), so the attacker must already control the victim's mailbox, which also allows a Devise password reset. What the attacker actually gains beyond that is an MFA bypass and a provider identity that stays on the account.
a.fix_direction: Report upstream to XIVAuth. Do not auto-link by email at sign-in: require the owner to be signed in (bind path :71-95), or run the MFA challenge and an email notice before the merge completes. On our side the impact can only be narrowed, for example by re-verifying moderator actions; no repo change closes it.
a.preconditions: The attacker controls a Discord, GitHub or Twitch account whose verified email equals the victim's XIVAuth email: a compromised mailbox, or a stale verification on a lapsed domain. Patreon is excluded as a login provider (user.rb:136) and Steam supplies no email. The victim must have an oauth row with a discord_id. Moderator powers apply only if the victim is listed in MODERATOR_IDS.
a.evidence_excerpt: email = auth.dig(:info, :email); return nil if email.blank?; existing_user = User.find_for_database_authentication(email: email.downcase); existing_user&.add_social_identity(auth); existing_user  ->  :60-62 if @user.persisted? ... sign_in_and_redirect @user, event: :authentication
a.live_state_dependency: Which omniauth providers are enabled in XIVAuth's production credentials (User.omniauth_providers = Devise configs intersected with credentials[:oauth] keys). The verified-email gating in the GitHub and Twitch gems is not vendored in the clone.
a.variants: Sign-in through an already-linked identity (:102-106) also skips MFA, but that is SSO by design and not this finding. Whether the identity built at :113 persists depends on Devise trackable saving the user on sign-in, which autosaves the new has_many record; this is likely but not verified in vendored code.
a.already_covered_by: Not covered: no entry in docs/architecture/security-trade-offs.md or in the 2026-10-03 or 2026-10-15 positive controls or rejected suspicions. FINDING-014 (2026-10-03) is a different issue (the identity switch when linking Discord).

b.title: Upstream XIVAuth links a provider identity to an existing account by email match and signs in without MFA, so control of a victim's mailbox bypasses their MFA
b.deploy_unit: upstream XIVAuth a4e6693 (not a xivdyetools deploy unit); impact lands in oauth + presets-api
b.reachable_path: An attacker who already controls the victim's mailbox registers or verifies a Discord, GitHub or Twitch account with that address, then signs in to XIVAuth with it. find_user_by_authdata (:109-116) matches the user by email and builds the identity, and sso_signin (:60-62) calls sign_in_and_redirect with no MFA step. Through oauth this yields the victim's presets-api JWT.
b.why: The code does what the candidate says: it looks up the user by email at :111, builds the identity at :112 and signs in at :62. MFA runs only in sessions_controller.rb:136-140. The finding is narrower than written: every login provider returns only a verified email. Discord checks this at lib/omniauth/discord.rb:23, GitHub 2.0.1 with the user:email scope returns only a verified primary email, and Twitch Helix returns a verified email (the gem was not vendored, so these two rest on gem and API docs). Steam returns no email, and Patreon cannot be used to sign in (user.rb:136). The attacker therefore needs the victim's mailbox, and that alone already allows a Devise password reset. What remains is a bypass of the victim's MFA, plus no confirmation from the account owner. Signing in through an already-linked identity (:101-107) also skips MFA, which appears to be upstream's design.
b.fix_direction: Report upstream. When the email matches but no identity is linked, XIVAuth should refuse to sign in or ask the account owner to confirm the link. If the matched user has MFA enabled, it should run the MFA step before signing in. Nothing in xivdyetools needs to change: oauth cannot tell that an identity was auto-merged, so it can only narrow this, not fix it.
b.preconditions: The attacker controls the victim's email inbox. The victim's XIVAuth account has Discord linked and has a presets-api row. The impact goes beyond what a password reset already gives only if the victim has MFA enabled.
b.evidence_excerpt: omniauth_callbacks_controller.rb:109-116 `email = auth.dig(:info, :email) ... existing_user = User.find_for_database_authentication(email: email.downcase); existing_user&.add_social_identity(auth); existing_user`; :60-62 `if @user.persisted? ... sign_in_and_redirect @user`; devise.rb:262-274 sets the GitHub scope to user:email and the Twitch scope to user:read:email; discord.rb:23 `email: raw_info["verified"] ? raw_info["email"] : nil`.
b.live_state_dependency: Which login providers have credentials configured in production. omniauth_providers is the set of Devise providers that also have credential keys (user.rb:144). Whether Flipper user_signups is enabled does not matter, because this path matches an existing user.
b.already_covered_by: Not covered by security-trade-offs.md or by the 2026-10-03 or 2026-10-15 positive-control and rejected lists. FINDING-014 (2026-10-03) is a different issue: linking an identity changes the presets-api identity.
b.variants: Signing in through an existing linked identity (:101-107) also skips MFA, which appears to be upstream's design rather than a separate finding.

a.title: oauth never clears or re-checks a row's Discord link, so a Discord id once attached stays the presets-api identity after XIVAuth stops asserting it
a.reachable_path: An XIVAuth user whose oauth row once got snowflake D (via xivauth.ts:343-353 -> findOrCreateUser at xivauth.ts:386-390) keeps signing in through /auth/xivauth/callback after D is unlinked upstream (XIVAuth social_identities_controller.rb destroy). The row is found by xivauth_id (user-service.ts:73-77), attachIdentities keeps existing.discord_id (:182-200), and jwt-service.ts:141 mints discord_id=D, which presets-api uses as the acting id for edit/delete/vote/moderator checks.
a.why: Code matches the claim: :182-200 only fills an empty discord_id and has no branch that clears or compares it when linkedDiscordId is null or different; oauth exposes no unlink or account-delete route (index.ts:290-293 mounts only authorize/callback/xivauth/token). D's real owner signing in via Discord (callback.ts:239-244, xivauth_id null) lands on the same row through the discord_id lookup (:81-86) and cannot evict the stale xivauth_id; only a different XIVAuth account asserting D replaces it (:202-208). Impact is LOW because a harmful case needs a prior mis-link (candidate 01's precondition, or a temporary Discord-account compromise) and a legitimate link has no effect; not covered by security-trade-offs.md or either prior report (the 2026-10-03 gap2 evidence noted "never clears" only as a positive control against reverse takeover).
a.fix_direction: On XIVAuth sign-in, when the row's discord_id is set and upstream no longer asserts it (null or different), detach the XIVAuth link from that row (null its xivauth_id and give the XIVAuth account a fresh row) instead of minting the stale D. Keep the Discord-anchored row and its D intact so bans keyed on D cannot be shed by unlinking. Add tests for both the unlink and the re-link-elsewhere cases.
a.preconditions: The XIVAuth account must have once asserted D while signing in to xivdyetools, and D must later be unlinked upstream. For harm, the XIVAuth holder must not be D's owner (upstream email auto-merge mis-link per candidate 01, or a temporarily compromised Discord account linked and then unlinked).
a.evidence_excerpt: user-service.ts:182-183 `let discordId = existing.discord_id; if (!existing.discord_id && discord_id) {` (no else branch); jwt-service.ts:141 `discord_id: user.discord_id ?? undefined`
a.live_state_dependency: Whether any production users row is currently in this stale state requires reading prod D1 xivdyetools-users and comparing it against XIVAuth links, which the repo does not show.
a.already_covered_by: Not covered. 2026-10-03 evidence review-gap2-identity-link-blast-radius.md:24 recorded the same never-clear behavior as a positive control, not as a finding; it is not in either report's Positive controls / Rejected lists.
a.variants: Same stickiness on the race-fallback path user-service.ts:235-247 (keeps existing.discord_id). Same effect through callback.ts:239-244: a Discord sign-in reuses the stale-linked row.

b.title: oauth never clears a row's Discord link when XIVAuth stops asserting it: the unlinked Discord id is still stored and minted. The impersonation amplifier the candidate claims is narrower than stated.
b.reachable_path: An XIVAuth user who has signed in once with Discord linked, and then unlinks Discord or stops sharing it, signs in again. xivauth.ts:386-395 passes discord_id=null, attachIdentities keeps existing.discord_id (user-service.ts:182-200), and jwt-service.ts:141 mints it again.
b.why: The code fact is real. Nothing clears or re-checks discord_id when the asserted value is null, and no test covers that case (user-service.test.ts:246-365 covers only the never-overwrite and owned-id cases). "Permanent impersonation" is overstated on three counts. (1) In candidate 01 the attacker gets into the victim's own XIVAuth row, so the stickiness gives the attacker nothing beyond that access. (2) The direction where it matters, the victim's Discord attached to an attacker-owned XIVAuth account, is blocked upstream by Devise confirmable, and the reviewer's own evidence says so. Locally it is also refused whenever that Discord id already has a row (user-service.ts:186-195). (3) The Discord owner can evict the stale xivauth_id by linking the id to their own XIVAuth account and signing in (user-service.ts:202-208). What remains reachable for every user is retention: the Discord id stays stored and minted after the user withdraws it upstream. That conflicts with the "collect nothing personal" stance and with PRIVACY.md:88, which says the record holds the Discord id only while the XIVAuth account is linked.
b.fix_direction: On an XIVAuth sign-in that asserts no Discord identity (or a different one), clear discord_id on a row where xivauth_id equals the caller, but only when the row was not created by a Discord sign-in. Track that origin in a link_source column, or keep a Discord-first row as is. Add a test that pins the null-assertion case.
b.evidence_excerpt: user-service.ts:182-183 `let discordId = existing.discord_id; if (!existing.discord_id && discord_id) {` has no else branch. xivauth.ts:346-353 sets linkedDiscordId=null when there is no discord identity. The eviction path is user-service.ts:202-208. The owned-id refusal is user-service.ts:186-195.
b.preconditions: Retention: any XIVAuth user who once linked Discord and later unlinks it or deselects it. Impersonation: someone else's Discord must first be mis-attached upstream to an XIVAuth account the attacker controls, while that Discord id has no local row yet. There is no confirmed path to that today.
b.live_state_dependency: Upstream XIVAuth behaviour (Devise confirmable order at a4e6693, and whether the GitHub and Twitch strategies verify email) decides whether the impersonation precondition is reachable at all.
b.already_covered_by: Partly noted in docs/audits/2026-10-03-security/evidence/review-gap2-identity-link-blast-radius.md (rejected suspicion: "Reverse direction (unlink...): no such flow exists in oauth"). That note is reviewer evidence only and is not in that audit report's Positive controls / Rejected list, so it does not bar this finding.
b.variants: The same stickiness applies on the Discord path: callback.ts:239 always asserts Discord's own id, so it is moot there. The race fallback at user-service.ts:242-247 also keeps existing.discord_id.

In the same change, update the pin in tests/wrangler-config.test.ts:106, presets-api CLAUDE.md:313, DOMAIN_DEPRECATION.md:52, environment-variables.md:181 and projects/presets-api/overview.md:260.

v3.title: presets-api production CORS lists xiv-colorexplorer.pages.dev. It is the live production Pages project's own subdomain, and a claimed origin would gain nothing under Bearer-only auth.

Their page would then get CORS-readable responses from api.xivdyetools.app, but only for requests carrying a Bearer token it already holds, which it could send from curl without CORS.

It is the subdomain of the live production Pages project (deploy-web-app.yml:76 `--project-name=xivdyetools`, comment at :84-88), so the takeover precondition is not met. The 2026-10-03 audit weighed this exact item and rejected it as hygiene only; it was filed as INFO in 08-21 and 08-29. Opinion A agrees on every fact but calls it INFO PARTIAL, which would re-file a no-effect note that has already been decided.

a.title: /preset favorite list fans out up to 50 userless presets-api reads that skip both presets-api limiters
a.reachable_path: Any Discord user who has added up to 50 favorites (MAX_PRESET_FAVORITES, preset-favorites.ts:34) runs a signed `/preset favorite list` interaction. processFavoriteList (preset.ts:1310-1312) then issues one `Promise.all` of up to 50 `presetApi.getPreset` calls over the PRESETS_API service binding, each with no X-User-Discord-ID.
a.why: getPreset (preset-api.ts:237-239) passes no userDiscordId, so request() (preset-api.ts:93-98) sends no identity header. presets-api's IP limiter returns early when there is no CF-Connecting-IP (rate-limit.ts:138-140), and the per-user limiter returns early when actingUserId is undefined (rate-limit.ts:158-160, :110-114; auth.ts:282 sets userDiscordId to undefined for a userless bot call). The only bound is discord-worker's per-user `preset` tier of 10/min (configs.ts:83, applied at index.ts:952-965), so each account can drive about 500 primary-key D1 reads per minute, and this scales with the number of accounts. The impact is load amplification only: no data is exposed and the reads are cheap single-row lookups, so this is LOW hardening.
a.preconditions: You need a Discord account that can use the bot and has favorited up to 50 presets, which takes up to 50 prior /preset favorite add commands at 10/min. This is real as described. The presets-api reviewer recorded the binding skip as by design (review-presets-api-routes.md:7,46), but the rate-limit.ts comment says binding traffic is "limited per-user instead", and that never covers userless reads.
a.variants: This is the same userless-read pattern as the other single getPreset/getPresets calls in preset.ts (e.g. :975, :206), but only favorite list multiplies it by 50 per command. Favorite autocomplete was already de-fanned by OPT-007 (v2 entries keep the names).
a.fix_direction: Render the list from the v2 denormalized {id,name} entries, or add a batch `GET /presets?ids=` endpoint so the command makes one call. Failing that, cap the concurrency and send the acting userDiscordId so presets-api's per-user limiter counts these reads.
a.already_covered_by: Not covered: no trade-off entry in security-trade-offs.md and nothing in the 2026-10-03 or 2026-10-15 positive controls or rejected lists. The presets-api route review only notes the general binding skip as design.
a.live_state_dependency: This assumes the production RL_* bindings enforce the 10/min preset tier. If they are unbound, the KV fallback applies the same nominal limit, but it is eventually consistent.

a.title: Ban keyed on one identity leaves the author's other-identity presets public and approvable
a.reachable_path: An XIVAuth-only user submits presets on the web (keyed by oauth sub UUID), links Discord, then submits through the bot (keyed by snowflake) before the next web sign-in runs refresh-author. A moderator bans the snowflake: hideUserPresetsStatement (ban-service.ts:684-691) hides only author_discord_id = snowflake, so the UUID-keyed approved presets stay public and isPresetAuthorBanned (:38-48) still lets pending UUID-keyed ones be approved.
a.why: All three code facts hold: the hide UPDATE binds the single target id (:686-691), banUser fills xivauth_id only when the target is itself a UUID (:489), and the MOD-4 approval guard joins banned_users on p.author_discord_id only (:42), so a snowflake ban never matches UUID-keyed rows. After the ban, presets.ts:371-379 skips the re-key and identity-rekey-service.ts NOT_BANNED (:22-25) blocks it too, so the split stays in place for good. The impact is bounded: requireNotBanned (presets-api ban-check.ts:147) checks userDiscordId, jwtSub and jwtDiscordId, so the banned user cannot post, edit or vote from either client; what remains is old content staying visible and a moderator-approval guard that does not fire. That is LOW, and the split identity is a narrow precondition.
a.fix_direction: moderation-worker cannot resolve the sub-to-snowflake link itself (it has no oauth binding). Have the ban flow ask presets-api or oauth for the linked ids over a service binding and hide and match both. Otherwise show the moderator every author id sharing that author_name or linked identity in the ban confirmation, and add a test for the snowflake-ban-with-UUID-presets case.
a.policy: NONE: discord-worker/PRIVACY_POLICY.md section 'Moderation Records' and web-app PRIVACY.md describe only what a ban record stores. They do not promise that every preset of a banned person is hidden, so no policy text is false.
a.preconditions: The author must hold presets under both the XIVAuth sub UUID and the Discord snowflake at ban time. That happens when they submit on the web while XIVAuth-only, link Discord, and submit through the bot before any web sign-in runs refresh-author, or when they never sign in on the web again after linking. The moderator must also ban only the snowflake. How often such split identities exist in production D1 has not been checked.
a.live_state_dependency: Whether any production author currently holds presets under both a UUID and a snowflake (prod D1 xivdyetools-presets), which cannot be read from the repo.
a.already_covered_by: Not covered. This is the reverse direction of 2026-10-03 FINDING-014, which handled a UUID ban lapsing after a link. Its REMEDIATION_PLAN.md:187 notes that moderation-worker 'cannot look up a linked Discord id' but files no finding for the snowflake-ban case. It is not in security-trade-offs.md or in either report's positive controls or rejected suspicions.
a.variants: The worker's other single-id moderation queries have the same keying: countHiddenPresets (:662-674) and restoreUserPresetsStatement (:705-718). They are consistent with the hide, so an unban restores what the ban hid. The confirmation embed counts only the target id's presets.

AND status = 'approved' .bind(now, discordId); :489 const xivAuthId = isXivAuthUuid(discordId) ? discordId : null; :42 ON (b.discord_id = p.author_discord_id OR b.xivauth_id = p.author_discord_id)

b.title: A ban on one id does not hide presets the same person filed under a second id the database has never linked
b.reachable_path: An XIVAuth-only web user files presets keyed by the oauth sub UUID. The same person also files through the Discord bot (keyed by snowflake) and is never re-keyed: the link is only stamped at an XIVAuth web login (oauth user-service.ts:183-199), and that login immediately calls refresh-author (web-app auth-service.ts:531). A moderator then bans the snowflake, and the UUID-keyed presets stay approved, while the pending ones can still be approved (isPresetAuthorBanned, ban-service.ts:35-51, only matches p.author_discord_id against the ban row's two columns).
b.why: The code reads as the claim says: hideUserPresetsStatement (ban-service.ts:683-688) and isPresetAuthorBanned key only on the target id, and xivauth_id is filled only for a UUID target (:489). In the claimed window, though, no database moderation-worker or presets-api can read links the two ids, so this is the same as one person holding two accounts, which FINDING-014 (2026-10-03) already rated LOW because a banned user can evade with a fresh Discord account. The banned person is fully blocked: requireNotBanned checks userDiscordId, jwtSub and jwtDiscordId (presets-api ban-check.ts:147), and PATCH /refresh-author sits behind it (presets.ts:131). What is left is moderation completeness for content moderators already approved or still have to approve, and no policy text promises that a ban hides every preset (discord-worker PRIVACY_POLICY.md Moderation Records).

Then hide and match on both ids in hideUserPresetsStatement and isPresetAuthorBanned. Alternatively, have the ban confirmation embed list presets under any id known to be linked.
b.already_covered_by: Residual of docs/audits/2026-10-03-security/findings/FINDING-014.md (LOW, accepted reasoning: a banned user can already evade with a fresh Discord account); not in the trade-offs doc or a Rejected-suspicions list.

a.title: /glamour embed truncation cannot fit an oversized notes tail, and the failed success-path edit goes unrecorded (robustness, not attacker-reachable)
a.reachable_path: A signed Discord user runs /glamour with a .chara file. bot-logic builds `tail` from item names that api-worker resolves from XIVAPI or its bundled tables (game data). The user's file supplies only model IDs, which api-worker bounds to 0..65535, so the user cannot make those names long.
a.why: Each part of the mechanics checks out. EMBED_BUDGET is 4000 (glamour.ts:193). When tail.length > 3996, lastIndexOf receives a negative fromIndex, which it clamps to 0, and returns -1 (or 0), so slice(0,-1) keeps almost all of the body (glamour.ts:606-607); the same happens when the body has no newline before the cut point. The tail itself is never capped, so even correct math could not fit it. The success-path edit at apps/discord-worker/src/handlers/commands/glamour.ts:185 ignores the boolean from safeEditOriginalResponse (discord-api.ts:259-285), so the trace stays `ok`; the helper still writes a console.error, but this worker has observability off. Real game item names keep the tail around 2.6k characters, so reaching the overflow needs malformed upstream data that no attacker controls. The only effect is that the requesting user's own reply fails, with no data exposure, so this is a robustness bug (INFO), not the claimed LOW.
a.fix_direction: Cap the tail first (truncate the notes at a line boundary to leave about 1k for the body). Clamp the cut index with Math.max(0, ...) and fall back to a hard slice when lastIndexOf returns -1. Have the success-path edit check safeEditOriginalResponse's result and call markCommandOutcome(interaction, 'render') on false.
a.preconditions: Upstream item names (XIVAPI, or api-worker's bundled ko/zh tables) would have to be abnormally long; api-worker's cleanName (xivapi.ts:96) applies no length cap. An attacker cannot trigger this through the .chara file alone.
a.variants: The ignored safeEditOriginalResponse return is a project-wide pattern, not specific to /glamour: success-path edits in accessibility.ts, comparison.ts, contrast.ts, dye.ts, extractor.ts, gradient.ts, harmony.ts, mixer-v4.ts and budget.ts also discard it. Only manual.ts:407 checks it.
a.evidence_excerpt: glamour.ts:193 `const EMBED_BUDGET = 4000;` ; glamour.ts:606-607 `if (body.length + tail.length + 2 > EMBED_BUDGET) { body = `${body.slice(0, body.lastIndexOf('\n', EMBED_BUDGET - tail.length - 4))}\n…`; }` ; handlers/commands/glamour.ts:185 `await safeEditOriginalResponse(...)` with the boolean result discarded.
a.live_state_dependency: Whether XIVAPI ever serves an abnormally long item name. The repo's bundled name tables and real game data keep names short.

b.title: /glamour embed truncation underflows when the notes tail is near EMBED_BUDGET; success-path edit result unchecked (robustness, not attacker-reachable)
b.reachable_path: A signed /glamour interaction with a .chara file reaches executeGlamour, but the file only selects item IDs; the tail text is built from XIVAPI game-data names returned by api-worker's resolve. Pushing tail.length past ~3996 (EMBED_BUDGET=4000, glamour.ts:193) needs abnormal upstream names, which no Discord user controls; a user maximizing pieces with long real names stays near 2-3k.
b.why: The math is real: with EMBED_BUDGET - tail.length - 4 negative (or no newline before that index), lastIndexOf returns -1 and body.slice(0,-1) keeps almost the whole body, so the description can exceed Discord's 4096 and the edit is refused; apps/discord-worker/src/handlers/commands/glamour.ts:185 ignores safeEditOriginalResponse's boolean (it only console.errors, discord-api.ts:259-284), leaving the user on "thinking" with no failure outcome marked. But the trigger is trusted third-party game data, not client input, and the only effect is the requester's own reply failing, so there is no security impact beyond a robustness gap. Existing test (glamour.test.ts:654) pins only the normal truncation case.
b.fix_direction: Clamp the cut index: compute room = EMBED_BUDGET - tail.length - 4; if room <= 0 drop the body (or truncate the tail too), else use Math.max(0, lastIndexOf) and hard-slice to room. In the handler, check the boolean from safeEditOriginalResponse and call fail()/markCommandOutcome on false. Add a test with an oversized tail.
b.preconditions: Upstream XIVAPI (via api-worker /v1/chara/resolve, names only cleaned by cleanName at apps/api-worker/src/chara/xivapi.ts:96, no length cap) returns item names long enough that the notes tail exceeds ~3996 chars.
b.evidence_excerpt: glamour.ts:606-607 `if (body.length + tail.length + 2 > EMBED_BUDGET) { body = `${body.slice(0, body.lastIndexOf('\n', EMBED_BUDGET - tail.length - 4))}\n…`; }`; handler glamour.ts:185 `await safeEditOriginalResponse(...)` return value discarded.
b.variants: Same unchecked-boolean pattern may exist on other success-path safeEditOriginalResponse calls; out of scope for G37.
b.live_state_dependency: Content of XIVAPI item names at request time (third-party).

a.title: Page-side worker-answer validator accepts any 256-unit string as tribe, then casts it to SubRace for the swatch config and clan lookup (defense in depth only)
a.reachable_path: No external sender can reach it. The tribe comes from the first-party, same-origin inspection worker (chara-inspection-service.ts:291). That worker uses xivcharakit, which enumerates tribe against TRIBES (dist/index.js:32-49, 190; this list is identical to SubRace), and core projects tribe only when state==='valid' (packages/core/src/services/chara/chara-library.ts:258).
a.why: readCharacter checks race and gender against enums. It checks tribe only with isLabelOrNull (protocol.ts:415-421, 739) and casts it at :757. CharaSessionService.getTribeAndGender (chara-session-service.ts:47-52) returns it as SubRace, and ConfigController.pinToCharaFile (config-controller.ts:218-223) and swatch-tool.ts:414-417 use it without the toSubRace check at swatch-tool.ts:402. chara-file-card.ts:316-317 indexes SUBRACE_TO_CLAN_KEY with it. Only a defective first-party worker or core could put a non-SubRace value there, and the worst effect is a wrong clan label or a bad race value in the user's own swatch config in localStorage. That value is read back through toSubRace at swatch-tool.ts:402. The value is game data, not personal data.
a.fix_direction: In readCharacter, check tribe with `(tribe === null || isIn(SUBRACES, tribe))`, as race and gender already are, and drop the cast at :757. Add a protocol test that rejects an unknown tribe.
a.preconditions: A defective or compromised first-party worker bundle, or a core or xivcharakit regression, would have to emit a tribe that is not a SubRace. No user-supplied .chara file can do this today, because xivcharakit enumerates tribe and core keeps it only when state==='valid'.

a.title: v2 bot signature binds URL pathname only; GET query string (status/search/sort/page/limit) is unsigned
a.reachable_path: discord-worker request() signs `new URL(...).pathname` (preset-api.ts:120), and getPresets (preset-api.ts:215-229) appends the filters as a query string. presets-api authMiddleware verifies against `new URL(c.req.url).pathname` (apps/presets-api/src/middleware/auth.ts:313-323). Rewriting the query needs someone inside the PRESETS_API service binding (wrangler.toml:30/154), which no outside party can reach.
a.why: Confirmed: canonicalV2 (packages/auth/src/hmac.ts:280-291) covers method, path, body hash, timestamp, nonce and identity, but never the query string, and both sides agree on the pathname. No attack follows. The request travels the service binding in both environments. Each nonce is single-use (isFreshBotNonce, 120 s KV) inside a 60 s window. The one query field that matters for authorization, status, is gated by isModerator, which comes from the signed identity (presets.ts:235-239), and getPresets sends no user identity.
a.fix_direction: Optional hardening: bind a canonical query (the sorted `url.search`) into canonicalV2 as a v3 field and update both bots and presets-api together. Otherwise document in hmac.ts that query parameters must never decide authorization.
a.preconditions: To matter, an attacker would need to sit inside the service binding, or the PRESETS_API_URL fallback would have to be used without the binding while TLS is intercepted. The attacker would also have to beat the single-use nonce check and the 60 s window. And a query parameter would have to become relevant to authorization beyond the identity-gated status filter.
a.live_state_dependency: This assumes the deployed production worker has the PRESETS_API service binding attached, as wrangler.toml:154 declares, so the URL fallback is never used.
a.variants: moderation-worker/src/services/preset-api.ts signs requests with the same createBotSignatureV2 pathname-only canonical, so it has the same property.

a.title: OAuth state is HMAC'd with JWT_SECRET (the JWT signing key) with no domain separation: latent cross-protocol risk, not exploitable today
a.reachable_path: Any client can call GET /auth/discord or /auth/xivauth with its own state, code_challenge and return_path (bounded by validateStateParam/validateReturnPath, oauth-flow.ts:166-186). The worker answers with HMAC-SHA256(JWT_SECRET, base64url(JSON)) via signState (oauth-flow.ts:203), which travels in the provider redirect URL.
a.why: The facts check out: signState (state-signing.ts:35-40) and signPayload (jwt-service.ts:83-84) both call signJwtData = hmacSign with the same JWT_SECRET, with no prefix or derived subkey. It is not exploitable. The state signing input is base64url and never contains '.', while a JWT signing input always does. Every JWT verifier requires exactly 3 parts (packages/auth/src/jwt.ts:116-117, 139-140), verifyState requires exactly 2 (state-signing.ts:61), and HMAC as a PRF leaks nothing about the key to someone who can request signatures. The only other JWT_SECRET consumer is presets-api's JWT verify (auth.ts:100), so the risk is latent: it becomes real only if a future HMAC(JWT_SECRET) use signs data with no dots.
a.fix_direction: Derive a separate state key, for example HMAC(JWT_SECRET, "oauth-state-v1"), or sign "state.v1:" + encodedState, in signState and verifyState. During the 10-minute state TTL, also accept the old signature (or just accept that in-flight logins fail once at deploy).
a.rotation: None needed: the key is not exposed, and the oracle reveals nothing about JWT_SECRET.
a.preconditions: None to reach the oracle. Exploitation would need a future feature that HMACs data under JWT_SECRET whose format matches a state (2 dot-separated parts) or a JWT-verifiable structure. No such feature exists in the tracked code.
a.evidence_excerpt: state-signing.ts:37-38 `const encodedState = base64UrlEncode(json); const signature = await signJwtData(encodedState, secret);` / jwt-service.ts:53-54 `signJwtData(data, secret) { return hmacSign(data, secret); }` / packages/auth/src/jwt.ts:116-117 `if (parts.length !== 3)`
a.already_covered_by: Not covered. The 2026-10-03 review-oauth.md:29 lists HMAC-signed state as a positive control but never raises key reuse or domain separation, and security-trade-offs.md has no entry for it.
a.variants: verifyState (state-signing.ts:65) and verifyPkceStateBinding (pkce-binding.ts:66, called from callback.ts:119 and xivauth.ts:149) use the same key. A related latent issue noted at jwt-service.ts:170-176 (oauth-11): no `aud` claim is minted, so token kinds would also not be separated if JWT_SECRET were ever reused.

a.title: JWT and V2 bot signatures accept non-canonical encodings (signature malleability, no exploitable consumer)
a.reachable_path: A holder of a valid JWT can re-spell its signature segment (std alphabet, embedded whitespace, '=' padding, non-zero trailing bits). jwt.ts:160 decodes it with base64UrlDecodeBytes and crypto.subtle.verify accepts it. A captured V2 bot signature can likewise be upper-cased (hex.ts:23 accepts A-F), and hmac.ts:203 still verifies it.
a.why: base64UrlDecodeBytes (base64.ts:67-78, not :254; the file is 105 lines) only remaps -/_, pads, and calls the forgiving atob. A local probe confirmed atob drops whitespace and ignores trailing bits ("QUJ=" and "QUI=" decode the same). Only the signature segment is malleable, because the signed input at jwt.ts:156 is the raw header.payload text. No consumer keys anything on the raw token or signature string: revocation keys on jti (oauth token.ts:131, jwt-service.ts:235), and the presets-api replay cache keys on the required nonce (middleware/auth.ts:159-213), so a re-spelled replay is still refused. The result is hardening only, with no direct effect.
a.fix_direction: In base64UrlDecodeBytes, reject any input that does not match /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]*$/, has length%4==1, or fails the round trip base64UrlEncodeBytes(decoded)===input. In verifyBotSignatureV2/hmacVerifyHex, require lowercase hex (/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/) before verifying.
a.preconditions: The attacker already holds a valid JWT, or has captured a V2 signature with a still-unused nonce inside the 60 s window. Re-spelling gives no new capability unless a future consumer keys a cache, blacklist, or dedupe on the raw token or signature string.
a.evidence_excerpt: base64.ts:69 `let base64 = str.replace(/-/g, '+').replace(/_/g, '/');` ... :78 `const binary = atob(base64);`; hex.ts:23 `/^[0-9a-fA-F]*$/`
a.variants: hmac.ts:173 hmacVerify (base64url signature, used by the oauth state HMAC) has the same leniency; hmac.ts:203 hmacVerifyHex and verifyBotSignatureV2 accept upper-case hex.
a.already_covered_by: Not covered by the security-trade-offs doc or by the 2026-10-03 / 2026-10-15 positive controls (a grep for malleab/canonical found nothing).

a.title: GPOSERS text() regex is quadratic on long non-newline whitespace runs (no attacker-controlled input reaches it)
a.deploy_unit: core (consumed by bot-logic /glamour in discord-worker, and web-app glamour export)
a.reachable_path: Bot: a Discord user uploads a .chara to /glamour, but the strings passed to text() are item names (api-worker, from XIVAPI), dye names (core's bundled data) and acquisition lines (api-worker's bundled data/acquisition.en.json); none of them come from the file. Web: the user's own Acquisition textarea (glamour-sheet.ts:266-284), which is stored only in that user's StorageService (acquisition-edits.ts:42-49), so the only person it can slow down is the user who typed it.
a.why: At chara-gposers.ts:120 the code is `value?.replace(/\s*[\r\n]+\s*/g, ' ')`. It backtracks quadratically on a long whitespace run that has no newline: my scratch run took 1.4ms at 1k, 61ms at 8k and 1098ms at 32k characters. gposersGroups (lines 130-149) and gposersSameRings (line 124) apply it to the name, dye1, dye2 and acquisition fields. The callers are bot-logic glamour.ts:409 and web-app glamour-markdown.ts:84 / glamour-list-actions.ts:186, and none of their inputs can be controlled by another user (bundled tables, XIVAPI game names, or self-only local edits), so the effect is at most self-inflicted UI lag.

a.preconditions: To affect another user, an attacker would have to control the upstream XIVAPI item-name response that api-worker relays (apps/api-worker/src/chara/xivapi.ts:378) or the bundled acquisition JSON. Neither is within an attacker's reach, and game item names are short.
a.variants: gposersSameRings (chara-gposers.ts:124-126) runs the same text() on the ring names.
a.live_state_dependency: Whether XIVAPI could ever serve an item name with tens of kilobytes of whitespace. That is upstream state and can't be read from the repo.
a.evidence_excerpt: chara-gposers.ts:120 `return value?.replace(/\s*[\r\n]+\s*/g, ' ').trim() ?? '';`, timed in scratch at n=32768: 1098ms.

a.title: publish job grants id-token: write to every step, including pnpm install, turbo build and vitest runs of dev-tree code
a.deploy_unit: CI + repo settings (publish-packages.yml, npm trusted publisher for @xivdyetools/*)
a.reachable_path: A maintainer dispatches "Publish Packages to npm" on main. a.title: Telemetry blob8 'ver' is regex-validated, not allowlisted, so a sender can write about 10 free alphanumeric characters
a.reachable_path: A non-browser client POSTs a text/plain v1 batch to https://data.xivdyetools.app/v1/telemetry with a forged `Origin: https://xivdyetools.app`, at least one valid event, and `"ver":"1.0.0-abcdefghij"`. version() (schema.ts:129-133) passes it through VER_PATTERN, slices it to 16 characters, and parseTelemetryBatch (schema.ts:160-166, 181) writes it as blob8 on every point in the batch.
a.why: The facts check out. VER_PATTERN at schema.ts:62 (`/^\d+\.\d+\.\d+(?:-[0-9A-Za-z.]+)?$/`) with the 16-char clamp at :61/:131 is the only envelope field not checked through oneOf against an enum (locale, theme, vp and env use envelopeField at :161-165), so a "1.0.0-" prefix leaves 10 free [0-9A-Za-z.] characters. The real client only sends the build constant APP_VERSION (web-app constants.ts:39, telemetry-service.ts:195), so no user data is collected; the only effect is a sender putting a short token of its own choosing into its own datapoints, which makes this INFO. This is an unremediated carry-over of 2026-08-29 API-05 (same INFO grade). The code is already stricter than spec section 4, whose `/^\d+\.\d+\.\d+/` is unanchored at the end.

Update schema.test.ts:174 (the timestamped-prerelease case) and spec section 4 to match.
a.preconditions: The sender must spoof an accepted Origin (trivial outside a browser; see origin.ts and the FINDING-014 gate), must not send Sec-GPC: 1, must stay within the TELEMETRY_RATE_LIMITER bucket (240/60 s per IP), and must include at least one event that passes its schema, because blob8 is only written on a valid event's point.
a.already_covered_by: Not excluded: it is not in security-trade-offs.md or in the 2026-10-03 or 2026-10-15 positive controls / rejected suspicions. It repeats 2026-08-29 API-05 (docs/audits/2026-08-29-security/evidence/review-api-worker.md:131), which was never remediated.
a.evidence_excerpt: schema.ts:61-62 `const VER_MAX_LENGTH = 16; const VER_PATTERN = /^\d+\.\d+\.\d+(?:-[0-9A-Za-z.]+)?$/;` and :130-132 `typeof value === 'string' && VER_PATTERN.test(value) ? value.slice(0, VER_MAX_LENGTH) : INVALID`

a.title: Public /webhooks/preset-submission has no failed-auth throttle or binding-only check (FINDING-027 optional hardening not done)
a.reachable_path: Any internet client can POST to https://bot.xivdyetools.app/webhooks/preset-submission (wrangler.toml:122-129, custom_domain route) with arbitrary Authorization headers. Each guess passes CORS/requestId/logger/validateEnv/security-header middleware (index.ts:205-272), none of which throttles, and reaches timingSafeEqual at index.ts:325, which answers 401 with no limiter.
a.why: The code matches the claim: the only gates are the non-empty check (index.ts:303), the production length floor of 32 (index.ts:315-322, MIN_WEBHOOK_SECRET_LENGTH at utils/env-validation.ts:33) and the constant-time bearer compare (index.ts:325). checkRateLimit is used only for interactions (index.ts:954,1113), and no CF-Connecting-IP / binding-only check exists. With the 64-character secret rotated on 2026-10-03, online brute force is infeasible, so this is residual hardening only: the optional second bullet of 2026-10-03 FINDING-027's fix.
a.fix_direction: Reject requests that carry CF-Connecting-IP before the auth check, since presets-api reaches this route only through the DISCORD_WORKER service binding. Alternatively, put a worker-kit limiter keyed on IP in front of timingSafeEqual. Confirm first that no non-binding caller (for example a manual retry script) depends on the public route.
a.already_covered_by: Continuation of 2026-10-03 FINDING-027 (docs/audits/2026-10-03-security/findings/FINDING-027.md, Fix bullet 2, marked "Optionally"). The finding is not an accepted trade-off in security-trade-offs.md and not a rejected suspicion; the required length-floor part is fixed (8ecb878f).
a.preconditions: An attacker would need to guess a 64-character bearer secret online, one HTTP request per guess, which is impractical. The beta worker (top-level, workers_dev=true, wrangler.toml:16) gets no length floor, because that check runs only when ENVIRONMENT=production. Its exposure therefore depends on the beta secret's strength, and beta can only post to beta channels.
a.live_state_dependency: The production INTERNAL_WEBHOOK_SECRET is documented as 64 characters (rotated 2026-10-03), but it cannot be read back. The beta worker's secret length is unknown. Any Cloudflare zone-level WAF or rate-limiting rule on bot.xivdyetools.app is not visible from the repo.
a.evidence_excerpt: index.ts:325-328: if (!(await timingSafeEqual(authHeader, expectedAuth))) { logger.error('Webhook authentication failed'); return c.json({ error: 'Unauthorized' }, 401); }. No limiter and no CF-Connecting-IP check precede it.
a.variants: presets-api has the same webhook secret on the sending side. No other public bearer-only webhook routes were checked in this group.

a.title: Bidi/format characters not stripped from upstream item names (build-time ko/zh/ja tables and runtime XIVAPI names)

The runtime cleanName (src/chara/xivapi.ts:96) removes only U+00AD. bot-logic glamour.ts:385 `plain()` escapes only markdown characters, and skips sanitizeEmbedText (discord-markdown.ts:24 strips U+200B-200F/202A-202E) on purpose because the names are treated as trusted. A scan confirms 2 U+200F in item-names.ko.json (ids 1200 and 1238, "황‏토색") and 0 in ja/zh; both sit between Hangul letters, so today's effect is cosmetic: the two names fall back to English on the card, which item-name-coverage.test.ts:100 already allow-lists.

Optionally pin the Teamcraft source to a commit instead of the `staging` branch.

a.title: .chara Nickname/TypeName label truncation can leave ill-formed UTF-16 (cosmetic U+FFFD in the web card only)
a.reachable_path: A user loads their own .chara file in the web app, and the file has a Nickname or TypeName longer than 256 UTF-16 units with a surrogate pair at the cut, or a lone \ud800 escape. boundedLabel slices it and the web card shows a U+FFFD only to that same user (chara-file-card.ts:311, chara-sheet.ts:211, glamour-block.ts:1821).
a.why: At chara-library.ts:148, `value.slice(0, MAX_LABEL_UNITS)` cuts at a UTF-16 unit with no well-formedness check, so the fact is real. The claimed bot-reply effect is not: bot-logic removes the nickname right after projection (swatch.ts:260-266, glamour.ts:432), and it uses producer only through a substring token lookup (chara-identity.ts:81-85). Web telemetry likewise reduces producer to an enum (telemetry-service.ts:177-184). The only effect is a self-inflicted replacement glyph in the uploader's own browser, with no security or privacy impact.
a.fix_direction: Optional hardening: after slicing, drop a trailing high surrogate, or apply String.prototype.toWellFormed() to the bounded label (Intl.Segmenter if grapheme-safe cuts are wanted).
a.preconditions: The user has to supply a crafted or oversized Nickname/TypeName in their own .chara file. Nothing reaches another user, a log, storage or the bot output.
a.evidence_excerpt: chara-library.ts:146-149 `function boundedLabel(value) { if (typeof value !== 'string') return null; return value.length > MAX_LABEL_UNITS ? value.slice(0, MAX_LABEL_UNITS) : value; }`; bot-logic swatch.ts:265 `const { nickname, ...safeCharacter } = character;`
a.variants: The same slice applies to producer (TypeName, line 265) and nickname (line 269). Producer is only token-matched (bot) or enum-normalized (web telemetry), and the web chip upper-cases it, so it can show a stray U+FFFD at most.

a.title: Resolve-API response adopted without per-field shape validation (hardening only)
a.reachable_path: Only first-party api-worker's POST /v1/chara/resolve answer (or its upstream XIVAPI rows / its own KV cache) can supply the unvalidated fields; no browser user or internet client controls that body. A malformed iconId/itemId/name would then flow into glamour-block.ts:1001/1178/1328 style.backgroundImage, item-links.ts garlandToolsUrl/teamcraftUrl, and name rendering.
a.why: chara-resolve-service.ts:216-230 checks only success===true and that data.items is a non-null object, then spreads items/glasses/version into the session cache unchecked, unlike the field-by-field inspection-protocol validation. Server side, iconIdOf (api-worker/src/chara/xivapi.ts:175-182) admits only finite positive numbers, while rowId (xivapi.ts:243, raw.row_id) is TS-typed only, so a bad value needs XIVAPI or api-worker itself to misbehave. Sinks are bounded: CSSOM single-property assignment, fixed https:// prefixes on link builders (no scheme change), no innerHTML of resolved data in glamour-block (only a static icon at :588), and CSP img-src limits icon fetches to listed hosts.
a.fix_direction:
Validate the envelope like chara-inspection-protocol does: per slot accept null or {itemId: positive int, iconId: positive int|null, names: strings}, same for glasses; drop anything else to null.
Optionally also assert Number.isInteger(raw.row_id) in api-worker parseItemRow.
a.preconditions: api-worker (first-party), its chara KV cache, or upstream XIVAPI must emit a non-number iconId/itemId or a hostile name string; iconId is already filtered server-side, itemId (row_id) is not runtime-checked server-side but comes from XIVAPI's fixed base.
a.evidence_excerpt: chara-resolve-service.ts:226-230 `items: { ...outOfRange, ...envelope.data.items }, glasses: envelope.data.glasses ?? null`; glamour-block.ts:1001 `tile.style.backgroundImage = `url("${charaIconUrl(item.iconId)}")``; xivapi.ts:179 `if (typeof id === 'number' && Number.isFinite(id) && id > 0) return id;`; xivapi.ts:243 `rowId: raw.row_id,`
a.variants: Same unvalidated adoption reaches glamour-block.ts:1178 (glasses icon) and :1328 (twin rows), and item-links.ts garlandToolsUrl/teamcraftUrl (lines ~72-79).
a.live_state_dependency: None for the verdict; would only escalate if the deployed api-worker or its KV cache were compromised.

a.title: Published SwatchResult.character still carries the raw, uploader-controlled TypeName as `producer`
a.reachable_path: An uploader puts free text in the .chara `TypeName`. On /swatch, core's chara-library.ts:265 copies it as `producer` (capped at 256 UTF-16 units by boundedLabel, line 146), and toSwatchCharacter (swatch.ts:369) passes it through to `SwatchResult.character`, which is exported `@public` at bot-logic index.ts:127-128. No in-repo code reads `result.character`: apps/discord-worker/src/handlers/commands/swatch.ts:123-155 uses only svgString and embed, and stoat-worker never imports executeSwatch.
a.why: `SwatchCharacter = Omit<ResolvedCharaCharacter,'nickname'>` removes only the nickname. The raw TypeName stays in the published result, while the card itself shows only an allowlisted token (producerToken, chara-identity.ts:81-85, used at swatch.ts:479). Nothing in the repo reads this field, so it has no effect today. TypeName is a producer label, not a character name, so PRIVACY_POLICY.md:74 ("character names... never displayed") is not breached. The risk is limited to a future npm consumer echoing the free text.
a.fix_direction: In toSwatchCharacter, replace `producer` with `producerToken(producer)`, or omit it from SwatchCharacter, so the published result has the same allowlist as the card. This changes a published type, so bump bot-logic's major version (or ship a minor with a changelog note), and add a test that a hand-edited TypeName never shows up in `result.character`.
a.preconditions: The finding needs a downstream consumer of the published @xivdyetools/bot-logic API that prints or stores `result.character.producer`; no such consumer exists in the repo.
a.already_covered_by: Partly covered. docs/audits/2026-10-15-web-app-security/SECURITY_AUDIT_REPORT.md:71 lists as a positive control that the adapters do not serialize the parsed character into a Discord response, which matches today's behavior. That control does not address the published type's shape, which is the subject of this item.
a.evidence_excerpt: swatch.ts:102 `export type SwatchCharacter = Omit<ResolvedCharaCharacter, 'nickname'>;` swatch.ts:369-372 `const { issues, slots, ...rest } = character; return { ...rest, slots: ... }` (producer kept in rest). chara-library.ts:265 `producer: boundedLabel(inspection.metadata.TypeName.value)`
a.variants: Not a policy finding, so no locale variants. A related check: glamour.ts:441-549 reads `producer` and prints only producerToken(producer), and its result type does not return the character.

a.title: Third-party Teamcraft/XIVAPI strings enter acquisition.en.json without markup stripping (no reachable sink)
a.deploy_unit: api-worker (build-time script) feeding web-app and discord-worker/bot-logic
a.reachable_path: Only a maintainer running build-acquisition.ts against a poisoned upstream Teamcraft commit and committing the output could introduce a hostile string. The worker never fetches acquisition data at request time (apps/api-worker/src/chara/acquisition.ts:7, :24), so no internet client can influence the table.
a.why: The underlying fact is true: the builder writes `JSON.stringify(table)` at build-acquisition.ts:533/553 with no markup stripping. But every consumer escapes. The web-app renders the line only through textContent/input.value (chara-ui.ts:214 `el()`, glamour-sheet.ts:196 `preview.textContent`, :268 `field.value`), the Discord list escapes formatting via `plain()` (packages/bot-logic/src/commands/glamour.ts:384), the api-worker returns it as JSON, and no svg/og-worker card renders it.
